104. WHEN THE ENGINE SHIPS A ONE-DECISION FORM OF A REPEATED ACTION, THE GUIDE'S JOB BECOMES
    THE ARITHMETIC AND THE EMIT-GRAMMAR, NOT THE STOP. Lane N's repeat row moved deck123's loop
    from "take it again every window until a stop fires" to "name N once". The stop (M reaches
    L + C + 3) was already right; what the pilot lacked was N = (L + C + 3) - M as a formula and
    the one spelling the parser read. Of 10 takes, 4 lost their N: `N=17` and the row's own
    label echoed verbatim (`..., repeated N times, then stop`) each ran ONCE with no receipt,
    and a pilot that had computed 17 correctly three times watched the board not move
    (`seat-123-130.md` H1; `seat-engine-narration.md` D-2). Three of the four wrong spellings
    reproduced the ROW's wording rather than its example. So: where a rendered row carries a
    reply grammar, the guide quotes the grammar as an instruction about what to EMIT (#79),
    shows the exact form once, and names the wrong spellings the corpus produced. Boundary,
    per #99: state the spelling that IS read; never assert what the parser does NOT read — the
    parser's grammar is docketed to widen (wave-49 D3) and a negative sentence goes false the
    day it lands (boundary finding B1 this wave). The parser is the first owner of this defect;
    the guide line is the cheap side.

105. A WORKED EXAMPLE A GUIDE ASKS THE PILOT TO WRITE IS GIVEN AS A SHAPE WITH BLANKS, NEVER
    AS A FINISHED SENTENCE. Wave 47's 146-B added an accountability sentence with a quoted
    worked example ("nothing right now: the Command is entry 5, their board is empty and I
    control no creature ..."). This corpus the pilot emitted that sentence verbatim on menus
    that had NO Command row (`146 vs125` s83, s87 — `seat-146-152-162.md`, EDIT 146-E). #1
    forbids quoting text you intend to override; this is its positive-side twin: a finished
    sentence is COPIED, a shape is INSTANTIATED. Any sentence the guide wants in the reply is
    written as a template whose blanks the screen fills (`entry <number> <card>; it did not
    match because <printed fact>`). Cheap check, standing: grep the corpus for every sentence
    the guide contains in quotes; a verbatim hit in a reply on a screen where the sentence is
    false is the defect. deck125 shows the same mechanism working FOR the guide: 100% of its
    replies carry the guide's dictated plan line verbatim — which is exactly why #115 puts the
    gate's number inside that line.

106. BEFORE THE #102 REWRITE, READ EVERY VIOLATING REPLY FOR THE ARITHMETIC IT PERFORMED; IF
    THEY ALL PERFORM THE SAME WRONG ARITHMETIC, THE DEFECT IS A MISSING FACT, NOT A MISSING
    IMPERATIVE. deck146's converter rule failed a THIRD corpus with the render complete (7 of 7
    priced A-rows sent, a self-inflicted death from 4 life at `146 vs126` s72). The replies were
    not ignoring the rule — they computed it wrong the same way every time: "they gain 3 which
    Sanguine Bond drains from them, net 0". The pilot believed the converter is aimed at its
    CONTROLLER; the fold on the row said `their converter takes N off you`. No quantity of "stay
    home" moves a belief; one sentence that names the belief and refutes it in the fold's own
    words can (`deck146/skill.md` S-2, EDIT 146-A). Two more seats found the same shape from
    other directions: deck125's draw-is-damage stop held 0/9 on Revelations while the seat cast
    Elixir and Cancel under Forced Fruition + Underworld Dreams and took 7 then 14 — the pilot
    classifies by the guide's VOCABULARY, and a spell that makes you draw was not a "draw"
    (`deck125/skill.md` S3, W8); deck123 twice wrote "we have no blockers" under a printed
    `B1.` row and "Tutor to find a creature" one reply after writing "Tutor finds an
    enchantment" — the belief that a printed row does not bind (`deck123/skill.md` S4). So
    #102's step "quote the exact wrong sentences" is preceded by a diagnostic: extract the
    arithmetic or the classification each violating reply performed. Same wrong computation
    everywhere -> add the FACT (the direction, the composed price, "a row the screen prints IS
    the thing it says"), in the render's own words, and predict the belief-text metric. Only a
    scatter of different errors is an imperative problem.

107. A RENDERED COUNT IS NOT A RENDERED PREDICATE — WRITE THE SENTENCE THE NUMBER PROVES, AND
    ITS TENSE, BESIDE THE NUMBER. deck126's header read `of which 1 is a creature`; the rule
    said "when that reads exactly 1, cast Tribute"; twice the pilot wrote "keep Tribute to
    remove X if it becomes their only creature" and deferred, once into the loss (`126 vs123`
    s9 — `seat-125-126.md` D29 FAIL 0/2, EDIT F5). The executor matched the number and never
    resolved "1" into "only, now". deck162 is the mirror at the exception clause: "cast Master
    of the Feast whenever the opponent's line shows a creature" was cited as "MotF is the
    exception: it is a body that defends" on a board showing 0 creatures — the exception's NAME
    survived, its condition did not (`deck162/skill.md` S-3). So when a rule keys on a rendered
    number, write next to it the predicate the number establishes ("1 means the printed
    creature IS their only creature, in this window") and the tense ("now, not if it becomes");
    when a rule states an exception, restate its condition as the printed count in the same
    sentence and the negative case beside it (#98 applied to exceptions: "at 'of which 0 are
    creatures' it waits"). A deferral reply is a tense error, not a reading error, and it is
    countable: replies containing "if it becomes" about a creature the header already counts.

108. A CONDITIONED EXCEPTION TO AN ORDERED LIST IS A NUMBERED ENTRY AT THE RANK WHERE IT WINS,
    AND A MODAL CARD'S ENTRY CARRIES ITS MODES' CONDITIONS AS SCREEN FACTS. deck123's RULE 3
    said in prose "your number is 0 and theirs is 2 or more: that is the best Damnation there
    is. Take it"; the cast list ranked the makers 1-2 and removal 6; the pilot cast a maker into
    four attackers at 4 life and a dig at 0-vs-4, both game-deciding (`seat-123-130.md` L1/L2,
    EDIT A48-3 makes it entry 0). This is #70 (the exception lives above the imperative it
    excepts) and #92 (every conditional needs a rank) applied to the list itself, and it is
    the second seat in two waves to lose to a correct sentence with no rank. deck146 is the
    modal form: two waves of "Silverquill Command is always castable — there is always a
    playable pair of modes" produced 13 declines and then 7 Acererak-overs, and the s47 reply
    ENUMERATES the modes and finds none live on a board with 0 creatures either side and no
    MV<=2 creature in the graveyard — the sentence was false and the pilot knew it
    (`deck146/skill.md` S-4, EDIT 146-D). So a modal or conditional card's entry states each
    mode's condition as a fact the screen prints (their line shows a creature / your line shows
    a creature / the row's `{right now:}` names a returnable card) and the entry MOVES in the
    order when none is true. Extends #57 to the entry's rank.

109. BEFORE SCORING A HOLD OR GATE FRACTION, READ THE MENUS OF THE VIOLATIONS AND SPLIT THEM
    BY WHAT THE VIOLATION COST. Two seats, opposite conclusions from one method. deck126's
    "0 Lantern casts at {B} 2+" read FAIL 3/3 — but every one of the three windows had no
    higher-ranked castable row (the alternative was `Cast nothing`), and two of the games were
    won: the RULE was the defect and the fraction was the executor being right (EDIT F6
    reverses it). deck125's tap-out gate: six of ten violations were Elixir casts at {1} that
    cost nothing, and a rule broken repeatedly for free teaches the executor the rule is
    optional — it was then broken on the Staff cast that lost the game (`vs162` seq 27, Dreams
    resolved with no window the next turn; `deck125/skill.md` S2, S4, EDIT W10 scopes the gate
    to the spends that matter). Rule: a fraction is not a verdict until each violating window
    is read for (a) what else was on the menu and (b) what it cost in the NEXT window (the
    consequence trace, or its absence). Violations whose alternative was nothing are evidence
    against the rule; violations that cost nothing are exempted from the gate so the gate keeps
    its teeth where it matters. Report the split next wave, not the raw rate.

110. WHEN THE RENDER MARKS THE ANSWER, THE RULE'S FIRST LINE IS "ANSWER THE MARK"; THE
    DERIVATION STAYS ONLY FOR THE CASE WHERE THE MARK IS ABSENT, AND SAYS SO. Lane Q's `[<-
    most kills at any affordable X that costs you nothing]` sits on exactly the row deck130's
    STEP 1 + STEP 2 derive. The guide still opened with the derivation, and the one miss this
    corpus (`vs146` seq 47, X=6 taken over a marked X=2 four rows below) is the pilot stopping at
    STEP 1 and never reaching STEP 2 (`deck130/skill.md` S3, EDIT D48-5). #49 says gate on the
    rendered tag, never on a proxy; this is #49 applied to a multi-step PROCEDURE: when an
    emitter marks the row a procedure computes, the procedure's first sentence is the mark and
    the steps are demoted to the unmarked case. Corollary from the same window, engine-side:
    the mark sat on the LAST row under the owner's largest-first ordering while the option-1
    bias took row 1 — reported as R45 / wave-49 D14, not compensated in the guide.

111. A RULE KEYED TO ONE FORM OF A RENDERED TAG MUST NAME EVERY PRESENT FORM THE EMITTER CAN
    PRODUCE, AND ITS INPUT IS THE FACT ALL FORMS CARRY. deck130's keep-the-Commander-home rule
    read the COLLAPSED blocker tag (`they have N untapped creatures ... GANG BLOCK`). On a
    three-creature board the same tag is ENUMERATED (`[their untapped blockers: A (...); B (...);
    C (...)]`), no rung matched, and the Commander was sent into three "your attacker dies"
    prices and died (`vs152` seq 24; `deck130/skill.md` S2, EDIT D48-4). #82 says branch on a
    token's ABSENCE; #90 says name the string family; this closes the gap between them — a tag
    with two or more PRESENT shapes is silent on every shape the rule does not quote. Reviewer
    check: for every tag a rule quotes, list the emitter's shapes for it (the carry names them:
    collapsed / enumerated / the lane-P `most expensive to attack into` clause) and write the
    rule's input as the quantity every shape carries (here: the COUNT of blockers named). The
    engine-side half is D19/R27's one-canonical-substring ask; until it ships, the guide names
    the family.

112. FOR A DECK WHOSE MANA CAN COME FROM CREATURES OR WHOSE ACTIVATIONS TAP ATTACKERS, THE
    LETHAL COUNT IS THE FIRST CHECK OF THE TURN, ABOVE THE DEPLOY FLOOR, AND THE GUIDE OWNS THE
    PAYMENT. deck152 lost a game it had won on the screen: 25 power against 14 life and `of
    which 0 are creatures` on their line, and the lethal was spent in UPKEEP (Katilda's
    six-mana pump, 8 of 9 activations this corpus in Upkeep) and MAIN 1 (a Tracker cast whose
    `Those sources, one per untapped card:` line named `Intrepid Adversary {w}; Brutal Cathar
    {w}` — the attackers), before any attack rule was read (`152 vs162` s22-s26;
    `deck152/skill.md` S-2, S-3, EDIT 152-C). #71 put the lethal carve-out above absolutes and
    #56 put a race gate above the attack floor; both sit in the COMBAT section, and this turn
    was decided two phases earlier. Rule: such a guide carries the lethal count (printed
    untapped power vs their printed life, keyed to their creature count) as the first check of
    the TURN, says it outranks the deploy floor for that turn, and carries a rule keyed to the
    `Those sources` list: a creature named there is tapped by the next cast. deck130 supplies
    the authoring step for #71 in the same shape — for every absolute, name the printed
    quantity whose value would make obeying it fatal and put the comparison above it (its
    Starstorm absolute declined the only sweep that kept it alive at 8 life under 17 power;
    `deck130/skill.md` S1, EDIT D48-3). The render half (E-3: the row says `taps you out`, not
    `taps Intrepid Adversary`) is wave-49 D11; the guide's rule is written on the header line
    (#89 preference (b)) until the row carries it.

113. A CHECKLIST FOR A REPEATABLE ACTIVATION ENUMERATES THE PERMANENT'S OWN PRINTED STATE AND
    THE PAYMENT'S SOURCE, NOT ONLY WHETHER IT IS ALREADY DONE. deck146's Hive rule had CHECK 0
    (lethal), CHECK 1 (phase), CHECK 2 (already a creature), went 0 of 58 on the Upkeep problem
    it was written for — and then lost eight mana to a shape none of the checks covered: the
    source was `[tapped]` on the battlefield line and the only black source to pay it was the
    OTHER animated Hive, so both Hives ended `[tapped - cannot attack or block this turn]` and
    no attackers record was produced (`146 vs125` s63-s65; `deck146/skill.md` S-3, EDIT 146-C).
    The option row said nothing about either fact; the battlefield line and the `Those
    sources` line said both. Rule: for any activated ability on a permanent, the checks read
    the permanent's own tags (`[tapped]`, `[summoning sick]`) and the sources list, because both
    are rendered and the row is bare — until wave-49 D11 puts them on the row, at which point
    #89's row-first preference moves the check there. This and #112 are one lesson at two
    surfaces: the cost of an action includes what paying it TAPS.

114. A POSTURE RULE FOR A MATCHUP MECHANIC NAMES THE MECHANIC'S ESCALATED FORM FIRST, IN THE
    RENDER'S VOCABULARY, AND WRITES THE MECHANISM RATHER THAN THE SAFE-LOOKING BOARD. deck152's
    converter posture ("race it with your evasion") did what #78 asks — it selected among the
    options the price rules allowed and sent only the unpriced flier — and the flier killed the
    seat 20 -> 0 in one combat, because the board held BOTH `Sanguine Bond` and `Exquisite
    Blood` and on that board the unpriced damage IS the price (`152 vs126` s25; `deck152/skill.md`
    S-1, EDIT 152-A). The seat's own plan named both cards and still computed a finite race:
    the guide had a verdict for the single card and none for the pair, and the render described
    one direction of a two-card loop (R12, carried since wave 47, now a lost game — wave-49 D5).
    Rule: a matchup rule for a mechanic names its escalated form (the second card, the pair,
    the emblem) with the verdict there, keyed to both names on the battlefield line, BEFORE the
    default posture. deck126 shows the same defect at the safe-board end: its win-button attack
    rule fired "only if their side is empty", which never occurs against a real board, while
    the mechanism (lifelink pays on damage to a BLOCKER too) made the attack right into four
    untapped blockers and won the game (`seat-125-126.md` F7). Write the mechanism, not the
    board state that looks safe. Coverage-diff obligation (#81), and it is boundary finding B3
    this wave: deck146 faces the same opponent, paid the most to the single converter, and
    carries no sentence about the pair.

115. THE DICTATED PLAN SENTENCE IS THE GUIDE'S ONE GUARANTEED SURFACE IN THE REPLY — PUT THE
    GOVERNING NUMBER IN IT, AND A PLAN NAMES THE NEXT ACTION. Three seats converge. deck125:
    100% of replies carry the guide's plan line verbatim ("Answer their threats, resolve Staff
    of Nin, ping their face every turn"), and its tap-out gate had failed five waves from a
    section the pilot demonstrably does not re-read at the cast ask; W10 moves the gate INTO
    the plan line ("resolve Staff of Nin from a row reading leaves 5 or more") so the rule
    travels with every decision (`deck125/skill.md` S1). deck146 and deck162 both apply #102's
    plan-sentence check this wave with a named belief-text metric (146-A: "net 0"; 162-A:
    "stack the draw engines"). deck130 shows the failure mode of a plan with NO action in it:
    "The game is lost ... passing is the only legal action with no impact" rode 48 consecutive
    windows and produced a self-targeted Hammer of Bogardan and a blank X=12 Starstorm
    (`seat-123-130.md` L4, M3; EDIT D48-7). The reply protocol re-asks for a PLAN only when
    "part of yours is now done or false", and a verdict is never done and never false, so it is
    immortal. Rule: where a guide dictates a plan sentence, the number a failing gate depends
    on goes inside it; and every guide states that a PLAN is an action list — its next window's
    action, named — and that a verdict ("the game is lost") is not a plan. The core-prompt half
    (retire a carried plan that names no option) is wave-49 D7.

116. ADJUDICATE E1-ERA REPLIES BY THE LAST CODED LINE, READ THE REASONING BETWEEN THE FIRST AND
    THE LAST, AND TREAT `answer_replaced` RECORDS AS THE CORPUS'S OWN SPECIMEN SET OF THE PILOT
    ARGUING WITH A RULE. With the parser taking a final `CHOICE:` as the re-answer (21/21
    replacements this corpus resolved to the model's last coded line), a record's `choice` can
    differ from the reply's first line, and the reasoning in between is now the mechanism
    trace. Two of deck126's nine changed the play for the worse (`vs146` seq 43 ping -> pass;
    `vs130` seq 25 "cast nothing" -> Tribute at 0, via a hallucinated card name — the E1 hole
    docketed as wave-49 D2); scoring by the first line misses both, scoring by `choice` alone
    blames the guide for the second (`deck126/skill.md` S3). deck146's nine are six
    Acererak-vs-Command arguments, one Hive double-animation and one ATTACK line the parser did
    not honour (`deck146/skill.md` S-5). Rule: every seat counts `answer_replaced` per game and
    READS them; they are the cheapest input to #106's diagnostic and to #102's "read the
    override argument" step. Two counts are kept separate: replacements that rescued the
    model's own correction, and replacements that executed something not on the menu.

117. REPORT OFFERS BY PHASE AND WINDOWS BY KIND PER SEAT, SO A PHASE SKEW OR A STRUCTURALLY
    UNREACHABLE SECTION IS VISIBLE BEFORE ANYONE RE-FILES ITS PREDICTION. deck152's finding was
    a DISTRIBUTION, not an obedience rate: 9 Katilda activations, 8 in Upkeep — no compliance
    metric would have shown it (`deck152/skill.md` S-5). deck146's `becomes beholder` was
    offered 94 times, 58 in Upkeep, taken 0 in Upkeep — the guide fix worked and the 58 round
    trips are a cost line the engine should see (`deck146/general-suggestions.md` G-6).
    deck162 produced 0 `blockers` records in six games, so a whole section (zero-power walls,
    the LETHAL gate, rung 3) could not be scored for a second corpus (`deck162/skill.md` S-5;
    #21's structural-null rule). Rule, extending #63: the seat file carries, per deck, the
    window count by kind and the offer count by phase for every tap-cost or repeatable
    activation; a section with zero windows two corpora running is reported as
    unreachable-in-pool, not as a pending prediction.

118. "VIOLATED-UNPUNISHED" HAS A CEILING: AT THE THIRD CORPUS, #102 APPLIES EVEN WHEN NO GAME
    WAS LOST. #64 gave the verdict a name so favourable violations would not accumulate as
    loosening evidence. deck162's Rule 2 shows the other failure: three corpora at 3, 3 and 6
    breaks with 0 losses accumulated as NOTHING, and a rule broken 40% of the times it fires is
    not a rule the pilot has (`deck162/skill.md` S-2, EDIT 162-A). The `vs152` s6 reply PLANS
    "stack the remaining draw engines once Fate Unraveler is on the battlefield" while casting a
    Mine with none — the rule is in the plan and the answer breaks it, which is exactly #102's
    shape. So #102's trigger reads "third CORPUS of the identical failure with the fact
    rendered", not "third lost game": shrink, re-key to the printed count, plan-sentence check,
    belief-text metric. #45 still forbids LOOSENING on the same evidence; this is the opposite
    move.

119. A MULLIGAN SECTION IS ODDS REASONING THAT IS SATISFIABLE AT EVERY BOTTOM COUNT, AND A SET
    OF "NEVER BOTTOM" ABSOLUTES MUST BE JOINTLY SATISFIABLE AT THE SMALLEST KEEP. Three seats
    hit this in one corpus and all three re-wrote under the owner's ruling. deck146's STEP 1
    hard floor ("(keeping 5) or lower: KEEP, if the hand holds at least one land ... you are
    DONE") was broken on its first real test, on the argument "no white source", and the chain
    ran to a three-card hand of three lands after the pilot bottomed all four spells against
    its own plan (`146 vs152` seq 3-6, EDIT 146-F). deck162's "ONE LAND: ship it" collided with
    its own "already taken 1 mulligan -> LAST look: Keep" on exactly a one-land six, with no
    precedence stated (#97) — the seat split the one-land branch by LOOK with the odds at each
    and deleted both absolutes (EDIT 162-C). deck125's chain reached a 4-card keep and then a
    bottoming ask at which its three floors (three lands, last counter, last Path) could not
    all be satisfied with three cards to send — an UNSATISFIABLE rule set, and the executor
    chose freely (`vs126` seq 1-5, EDIT W13). Rule, superseding #66/#67's fixed stop look as a
    FLOOR while keeping their odds framing: each look is priced as a fresh seven shaved by one
    more card at the same land odds (state the deck's land count and colour-source count); the
    section says at each look what the ship buys and what it costs; the bottoming ask is the
    place the hand is BUILT — a preference ORDER (the lands that cover the cheapest spells,
    those spells, then the rest) that is satisfiable at any N, never a list of NEVERs that can
    exceed the cards in hand. Cross-guide obligation (#81): the pool converges on one doctrine
    — boundary finding B2 names the guides still carrying the floor text that failed.

**Supporting instances recorded, not amended.** deck162 S-4 (a "biggest" removal-target rule
names the engine class first — Ob Nixilis's -2 took a 1/1 token beside the Thraben Doomsayer
that then made twenty more): #17 applied to targets, adopted at the seat (162-B). deck123 S5
(Baka sacrificed Sigarda, its 6/6, to an edict at N=4 — one sample): WATCH; if a second N>=2
edict returns their best body, RULE 5's count gate is priced against the wrong opponent and is
re-derived from what Baka does. deck130's "Rorix is permanently tapped ... dead weight" read
under the opponent's Intruder Alarm: correct, the `doesn't untap` tag was read as written.


=====================================================================
EDITION AMENDMENTS — wave-49 (2026-08-27) — amendments 120-132
=====================================================================
Lessons from the wave-49 corpus review (sixth fair-hand corpus, `matchups-20260827-094106`,
binary master 7e94544f1: Vita fixes + lanes R/S/T/U; 42/42 seats carry a `gameend`, 21/21
natural — the "excluded deck123-vs-deck162 dead-loop" note in one seat file describes the
PREVIOUS run and is dropped). Each rule traces to a cited seat finding. Standing owner doctrine
(2026-08-26) governs every rule below: the REVIEWER owns the deck guide, synthesis owns this
skill and the general strategy, the core loop is the purpose; hard caps on the model's legal
choices are rejected; every guide rule is reasoned and odds-based, never a code-like floor.

120. THE GATE IS THE FIRST CLAUSE OF A DICTATED PLAN SENTENCE, THE ACTION FOLLOWS IT WITH
    "ONLY", AND A REPEATED-ACTION PLAN CARRIES ITS THREE NUMBERS AS BLANKS. #115 put the
    governing number INSIDE the plan sentence; this corpus shows WHERE in the sentence decides
    whether it fires. deck125's dictated line "resolve Staff of Nin from a row reading leaves 5
    or more" was echoed VERBATIM in the same reply that cast Staff off `taps you out` /
    `leaves 1` three times (`vs152` seq 23 — the loss; `vs146` seq 30; `vs130` seq 54): six
    corpora of one gate failing share the shape — the action fires, the qualifier trailing it
    is dropped (`deck125/skill.md` S1, EDIT W15). deck123's repeat-row stop held for exactly
    the windows whose PLAN still contained the number ("Create 20 more Vampires to reach 23
    total" -> x19 right) and failed on every window whose plan had lost it ("Attack with all
    creatures to win the game" -> x2, x25, x50, x120, x100 past the stop; `deck123/skill.md`
    S1, EDIT A49-1). Rule: a dictated plan sentence is written gate-first ("Keep a
    counterspell's mana open; Staff of Nin only from a row reading leaves 5 or more"), and a
    DECIDING bullet that restates the action WITHOUT the gate is the contradiction the executor
    resolves toward acting — cut it (#96). For a one-decision repeated action (#104) the plan
    shape carries three blanks the screen fills — the stop, the count now, this window's
    answer: `PLAN: stop at M = <L + C + 3>; M is <M> now; this window: <x<N> / pass>` (#105).
    Metric (#118's plan-text form): replies whose plan line carries the gate/all three numbers
    while the answer breaks it — 0/N is the pass; a reply without the numbers is a miss even
    when the answer was right.

121. WHEN A LANE SHIPS A COUNT ON THE ROW, RE-KEY EVERY RULE THAT DERIVED THAT QUANTITY IN THE
    SAME WAVE, ORDER ANY LIST BY WHAT IS A MENU ROW ON THE SEAT'S OWN TURN, AND SOFTEN AN
    ABSOLUTE WITH THE ROW'S COUNT RATHER THAN A PROSE EXCEPTION. Four seats, one move. Lane T
    put `{right now: they control N creatures - ...}` on every edict row and `{right now:
    destroys N of their creatures (K able to attack), M of yours}` on every sweeper row; deck123's
    RULE 5 still sent the pilot to the opponent's battlefield line for N and RULE 3 compared two
    "of which" counts with no notion of K (`deck123/skill.md` S2, EDITS A49-4/A49-5). deck125's
    "Revelation at Mana available: SIX or more" was broken five times for X=1/X=2 casts while
    the row printed `{X pricing: max affordable X=N}` (`deck125/skill.md` S3, EDIT W16).
    deck126's win-button list led with two combat triggers and a Staff the seat did not hold,
    and the executor, holding both enchantments with `Cast Tribute to Hunger {right now: they
    control 7 creatures}` on the menu, wrote "wait for the opponent to attack" for three
    windows (`vs152` seq 24-27; `deck126/skill.md` S1, EDIT F10). deck123's Damnation absolute
    was violated CORRECTLY at 0-vs-(a wall + a 1/1) and the softening used the row's own `(K
    able to attack)` instead of "unless they are walls" (`deck123/skill.md` S5). Rule,
    extending #49/#110: the review carry lists each lane's new strings; the reviewer's
    checklist item is "which rules derive a quantity a row now prints — re-key them to the
    row's literal, in this wave". A list of triggers leads with the entry that is a ROW on the
    seat's own turn, quotes its `{right now:}` string and says it needs nothing else. An
    exception to an absolute is keyed to a printed count, never to a card class in prose.

122. A SURVIVAL CARVE-OUT STATES THE POST-ACTION QUANTITY IT BETS ON, AND THE GUIDE WALKS THE
    SUBTRACTION ON THE ROW'S OWN LISTS. deck130's SURVIVAL FIRST ("their power >= your life ->
    take the X whose THEIRS list is longest, WHATEVER the YOURS list names") was obeyed at
    `vs152` seq 17-19 and killed the pilot's only blocker while the 6/6 that WAS the lethal
    survived every affordable X — the rule compared their total power to life when the question
    is their power AFTER the sweep (`deck130/skill.md` S1, EDIT D49-4; #71/#112's carve-out
    lacked its own falsifier). Rule: any "do X to survive" override names the printed threat
    that remains after X and requires it below the printed life; where the row prints kill
    lists, the guide shows the subtraction (THEIRS minus the kill list, summed against `Your
    life:`). Generalises: X buys survival only if the screen's remaining threat after X is below
    the screen's life; otherwise the override is a rule for dying one turn later.

123. AN "ALWAYS TAKE X" FOR A GAME-ENDING CARD CARRIES ITS COUNTER-SHAPE IN THE SAME PARAGRAPH,
    KEYED TO A SURFACE THE EXECUTOR CAN SEE, AND THE EXCEPTION FOLLOWS THE ABSOLUTE AND SAYS IT
    OUTRANKS IT. deck125's Emrakul line ("it outranks the tap-out gate ... take it anyway") was
    obeyed into a loss at 48 life with the win on the board: the opponent's next window printed
    `Tribute to Hunger ... Emrakul, the Aeons Torn is sacrificed, you gain 15` and took it, 48 ->
    -12 (`vs126` seq 117; `deck125/skill.md` S2, EDIT W14); the same edict shape cost 15 in a
    won game (`vs123` seq 55). The render had already said it — the LOOP clause ("ANY nonzero
    payment ... is fatal") was on the prompt. Rule, extending the obedient-absolutism pitfall:
    every finisher absolute names the one board where the finisher is the OPPONENT's card,
    keyed to the opponent battlefield line or the log ("Opponent cast <edict>"), placed AFTER
    the absolute with "this outranks the line above". Companion (#106): a finisher with a
    sacrifice/edict counter-shape is priced as a gift of its toughness on that board.

124. A ONE-ROW WINDOW IS A DECISION, THE PASS IS AN ANSWER, AND EVERY ABILITY THAT CAN TARGET
    ITS CONTROLLER'S OWN PERMANENTS GETS THE OWNER TAG AND THE PASS RULE — NOT ONLY THE ONE THAT
    BIT LAST. Two self-hits this corpus came from windows whose ONLY action row named the
    pilot's own permanent with a carried plan naming a target the window did not list
    (`130 vs146` seq 16 Spellbomb into its own Blastminer; `130 vs126` seq 38 Blastminer into its
    own Forgotten Cave) — the executor took the nearest row. The old "never a row tagged [your
    battlefield]" line existed for the Blastminer alone and was not generalised to the deck's
    other four target-taking abilities (`deck130/skill.md` S2, EDIT D49-5; #81 coverage). Rule:
    for every ability that can target its controller's permanents the guide states (a) the
    owner tag that marks a self-target (`[your battlefield]`) and (b) that a window of only such
    rows is answered `0 (pass)`; reviewer metric: rows taken whose target carries the owner
    tag. The engine half (a self-only window offered every priority; rows vanishing between
    main 1 and main 2) is on the docket; the guide rule stays correct after it ships.

125. A NAMED PAIR IS STATED AS TWO DIFFERENT NAMES; THE COLLAPSED FORM OF A DUPLICATE IS NAMED
    AS NOT THE PAIR; A COPY OF A NAME ALREADY ON YOUR LINE IS ENTRY NOTHING. `deck126 vs162` seq
    12: the seat cast a SECOND Exquisite Blood and wrote "Both enchantments are now on the
    battlefield" while Sanguine Bond was in its library, then waited for a loop that did not
    exist; the prompt was true (`Exquisite Blood #1-#2 x2`), the executor matched "two
    enchantments" to "both enchantments" (`deck126/skill.md` S2, EDIT F11; four second-Lantern
    casts the same corpus, F13). Rule: a guide whose win is a pair says "one <A> AND one <B>,
    two different names", quotes the render's duplicate form (`<A> #1-#2 x2`) as NOT the pair,
    and puts "a copy of a name already on your battlefield line" at the bottom of the cast list
    with the reason. The render half (a copy count on the cast row) is general R67.

126. AN ANECDOTE THAT MATCHES THE NEW FAILURE IS EVIDENCE THE RULE WAS KEYED TO THE STORY, NOT
    THE SURFACE — RE-KEY TO THE PRINTED STRING AND STATE THE ANSWER AS THE REPLY LINE. deck126's
    STEP 1 carried "Pride Guardian on Nadaar" as its example and the seat did Pride Guardian on
    Nadaar again (`vs146` seq 11, third corpus of the shape; `deck126/skill.md` S3, EDIT F14).
    Adds to #118's "shrink, re-key" step: when the failing window IS the guide's own worked
    example, the rule's key is wrong, not its evidence — re-key to the string the row prints ("a
    B-row whose EVERY parenthesis reads `your blocker dies, attacker lives`"), write the answer
    as the line the reply emits (`BLOCKS: none` when it is your only blocker), and cut the second
    anecdote; #105's template-with-blanks applies to the example that stays.

127. THE ENGINE'S AUTOMATIC CHOICES AT A SEAT ARE A REVIEW SURFACE: EVERY NARRATION LINE OF THE
    FORM `You <verb>ed <card>` WITH NO DECISION RECORD BEHIND IT IS LISTED FOR THE ENGINE SEAT.
    `123 vs152` seq 4 -> 5: the cleanup-step discard was made by the engine (`You discarded
    Intruder Alarm`) with no record between the two windows, and it discarded the deck's engine
    piece (`deck123/skill.md` S4; seat H2). No guide rule can fix a decision the pilot is not
    asked; the guide can only avoid creating the decision (A49-8's hand-size check), and that
    mitigation is written as a fact about the cards, never as a description of the engine's
    behaviour (#99/#103 — "the engine discards for you" is a sentence that goes false the day
    the ask is routed). Rule, extending #117: the seat file carries, per deck, the list of
    narrated actions with no matching decision record — the same shape as offers-by-phase, for
    actions taken without an offer.

128. THE #103 CHECK HAS A MECHANICAL STEP: EVERY QUOTED RENDER LITERAL OF FOUR OR MORE WORDS IN
    THE GUIDE IS GREPPED AGAINST THE SEAT'S PROMPTS, AND THE MISSES ARE REPORTED. deck123's RULE
    2 quoted "Put in Play with Marsh Flats targeting"; the emitter prints "Put a card onto the
    battlefield with Marsh Flats targeting" on every fetch window. The rule still worked because
    the pilot matched on the card name, but a literal no prompt contains is a false sentence
    waiting to matter (`deck123/skill.md` S3, EDIT A49-3). Rule: the reviewer extracts the
    guide's quoted strings and greps the corpus prompts before scoring any rule keyed to them;
    a quoted literal with zero hits is a defect of the guide whether or not the rule held. This
    is also how the wave-48 B1 shape (a guide asserting what the parser does NOT read) is caught
    before a lane makes it false.

129. DECKS WITH UPKEEP MANA SINKS CARRY A "YOUR UPKEEP" BLOCK THAT READS THE HAND AND THE LAND
    COUNT AND NAMES WHAT THE UPKEEP MUST LEAVE UNTAPPED. deck130's Hammer of Bogardan return is
    asked in upkeep, before the main-phase menu shows the body in hand; it was taken twice with
    Siege-Gang in hand and the lands to cast it (`vs146` seq 22, 28), and the Commander was never
    cast (`deck130/skill.md` S3, EDIT D49-2). #112 put the lethal count first in the turn for the
    same reason: mana spent in upkeep decides main. Rule: where a deck has a repeatable upkeep
    spend (Hammer's return, Katilda's pump, a Hive animation), the guide's upkeep section is the
    first thing read on the seat's own turn and is keyed to the hand line and the land count —
    "with <body> in hand and <N> lands, the upkeep sink is a pass". The offers-by-phase count
    (#117) is the metric.

130. CAST-ORDER RANK IS ALSO ORDER IN TIME: WHEN THE TOP ENTRY IS AN X SPELL OR A MANA-HUNGRY
    SPELL, THE LIST SAYS IT GOES FIRST IN THE TURN. `130 vs123` seq 22-29: entry 1 (Starstorm)
    and entry 3 (Molten Rain) were both castable; the pilot cast entry 3 first and then entry 1
    at the X the leftover mana allowed (X=1 against a Doomsayer the row said X=4 would kill; the
    Doomsayer made 25 Humans the next turn; `deck130/skill.md` S5, EDIT D49-3). "Take the FIRST
    line that matches" ranks within a window, not within a turn. Rule: any ordered cast list
    whose top entry's value scales with mana states the sequencing consequence in the entry
    ("it goes first in the turn — the X shrinks with every spell cast before it"), and the
    reviewer metric is "windows where a lower entry was cast before a castable X-entry".

131. A MULLIGAN SECTION IS CHECKED FOR SELF-CONSISTENCY BY CONSTRUCTING THE HANDS ITS SENTENCES
    DISAGREE ON. deck130 carried "mulligan only zero lands or all lands" beside "'would not
    cover any spell' is the one shape where seven can be worse than six"; at `vs123` seq 1 they
    disagreed on a one-land seven and the pilot picked one (`deck130/skill.md` S4, EDIT D49-1;
    #97, #119). Rule, the reviewer's check for #119: for each mulligan section construct four
    hands — 0 lands / 1 land without coverage / 1 land with coverage / all lands — at (keeping
    7), (keeping 6) and (keeping 4), and confirm every sentence in the section returns the same
    verdict for each; two sentences that disagree on any of the twelve are a defect before the
    corpus runs. The pool's floor text is gone at every seat this wave (deck130 D49-1, deck126
    F15 were the last two); this check keeps it from coming back as a contradiction instead.

132. A GUIDE EDIT PAIRED WITH A RENDER SHIP IS VALIDATED BY THE NON-RECURRENCE OF THE EXACT
    PRIOR LOSS — SAME SEAT, SAME OPPONENT, THE LOSING DECISION REPLAYED CORRECTLY — AND A SEAT
    THAT PRODUCES NO WINDOW FOR THAT REPLAY TWICE RUNNING REPORTS THE LANE UNTESTABLE-AT-THIS-
    SEAT. deck152's 152-A shipped beside lane U's `Both halves of a life LOOP` clause, and the
    wave-48 fatal attack (`152 vs126`, 20 -> 0) was replayed in the same matchup as `ATTACK:
    none` at both both-halves windows (s31, s40; `deck152/skill.md`). deck146's 146-A (#102/#106)
    has produced ZERO measurement windows for two corpora (`deck146/skill.md`). Rule: round-robin
    selfplay guarantees the matchup, so the preferred falsifier for a paired edit is the prior
    loss's own window, named in the prediction; a #102/#106 edit whose plan-text metric records
    NO WINDOW a second time is flagged UNTESTABLE-AT-THIS-SEAT in the seat file (neither
    confirmed nor refuted — #21's structural-null rule), and at a third no-window corpus the
    check moves to a permanent row annotation regardless, since the guide half cannot be
    validated. This is the converse of #118: #118 fires when the failure recurs; this fires when
    the test cannot.

**Supporting instances recorded, not amended.** deck162's Rule 2: #102's exhaustion clause
fired as written — the plan-text metric FAILED (`vs125` s8 plans "stack ... once a punisher is on
the battlefield" while casting Master with none; breaks 3/3/6/3 across four corpora, all in wins)
and the lane routes to the engine (R39 promoted, docket D15) with no fifth restatement
(`deck162/skill.md`) — a confirmation instance of #102/#118, not a change. deck125 W38's Cancel
at 2 life under Forced Fruition (the seat was dead to the next draw step regardless): a rule
break with no game in it, recorded, not re-worded. deck125's late-game land-drop declines (4/88
at 12+ lands, bare replies): first corpus, counted against 88 not assumed 100% (#87). deck152's
counter-spreading at its fourth corpus of ~2/13 (`vs126` s24/s30): #45/#64 hold, the remedy is a
row annotation (general R70), not guide text. deck126's three own-turn holds at `they control 3
creatures` with nothing else on the menu (`vs152` seq 16-18): recorded under F10's re-key. The
three `x1` repeat takes (the row used as a single): harmless, no rule.


=====================================================================
EDITION AMENDMENTS — wave-50 (2026-08-27) — amendments 133-151
=====================================================================
Lessons from the wave-50 corpus review (seventh fair-hand corpus, `matchups-20260827-115759`,
binary master 67aeffe45 = lanes V/W/X/Y/Z; **42/42 seats carry a `gameend`, 21/21 natural,
1,780 decisions, 3 fallbacks = 0.17%, all `stale_echo`, all one shape** — verified on disk by
this step; the "deck123-vs-deck162 dead-loop, excluded" note carried by one seat file describes
an older run and is dropped for the second wave running). Each rule traces to a cited seat
finding. Standing owner doctrine (2026-08-26) governs every rule below: the REVIEWER owns the
deck guide, synthesis owns this skill and the general strategy, the core loop is the purpose;
hard caps on the model's legal choices are rejected; every guide rule is reasoned and
odds-based, never a code-like floor. This wave's through-line: **the lanes closed the render
falsehoods and the engine-made decisions (Devour's pronoun, the cleanup discard, the
double-tap, the 34 KB row — all PASS by string), and what the guides lost to this corpus was
SEQUENCE — the executor quoting the guide's own rule in the same reply that broke it (#138,
#133), a rule keyed to the header after the row took the fact (#135), a new ask kind with no
section (#136), and a converter nobody counted (#149).**

133. UNDER THE ANSWER-FIRST PROTOCOL A DICTATED PLAN SHAPE'S BLANKS ARE FILLED BEFORE THE FIRST
    LINE IS WRITTEN, AND THE GUIDE SAYS SO. #120's three-blank plan worked: 9/9 repeat-row takes
    carried a stop number in the PLAN line (wave 49: 0/15) and the largest overshoot fell from
    300 to 28 (`deck123/skill.md` S1; seat-123-130 "the owner's question first"). The residual
    is structural, not textual: the CHOICE line is written first and the subtraction second, and
    four times the first line named a count (x0, x1, x3, x25) that the PLAN beneath it refused
    ("this window: pass" — `123 vs162` seq 35, `123 vs130` seq 31/46, `123 vs126` seq 32, the
    last 25 tokens past a stop of 30). The same commit-before-think shape appeared as prose at
    deck146: `146 vs123` seq 20 `CHOICE: 3 (Cast Soul Shatter)` on line one, 2,700 chars ending
    "I will cast Pelakka Predation", no second coded line, Soul Shatter cast into an empty board
    (seat-146-152-162 E-5). Rule: where the protocol commits on line one, a plan shape with
    blanks is introduced with the ORDER of the work — "do the subtraction before you write the
    first line; the CHOICE line is the plan's `this window:` blank, never a guess" — and the
    reviewer's metric is "replies whose CHOICE count (or named row) disagrees with the PLAN
    line's own answer", 0/N is the pass. The engine half (a `plan_choice_conflict` re-ask; a
    `decision_reversed_in_prose` counter) is docketed (wave-51 D4, D20); the guide half ships
    now because the protocol is the owner's and will not move.

134. A NAMED COUNT OF ZERO IS A PASS, AND EVERY GUIDE THAT TEACHES A COUNT GRAMMAR TEACHES THAT
    `x0` IS NOT ONE. `123 vs162` seq 35: `CHOICE: 2 (Create human with Thraben Doomsayer x0)` /
    `PLAN: Stop at M = 25. M is 26 now. Pass.` -> `ran 1 time (you named 0)`, `parse_note:
    repeat_count_under_two` (`deck123/skill.md` S2; seat-123-130 H1; engine seat D-3). The
    pilot used the row's own grammar to say "none" and the engine turned it into a take. Until
    the engine half ships (wave-51 D4: a count of 0 is a decline), any rule that teaches #104's
    count grammar states the pass answer literally beside it — "`CHOICE: 0 (pass)` — never
    `x0`" — one line, wherever the count is taught. Not a cap: the pass row is on every such
    window and is the thing the pilot meant.

135. AN ABSOLUTE ABOUT A CLASS ("EXACTLY ONE — WHATEVER IT IS", "ONLY EVER COSTS THE OPPONENT",
    "N = 1 IS THE CAST") IS AUDITED BY CONSTRUCTING THE CLASS'S LEAST-HARMFUL MEMBER AND THE
    DECK'S OWN EXCEPTION, AND THE CARVE-OUT IS KEYED TO THE PRINTED TAG. Three seats, one shape:
    deck126's Tribute-at-one rule reached ceiling and then spent the deck's only own-turn win
    trigger on a Shield Sphere `[defender]` (`vs162` seq 8), and the window that needed it
    (both halves out, two Fog Banks, 3 life, seq 23-24) had none (`deck126/skill.md` S1, F17);
    deck125's "your battlefield has no creatures, so a wipe only ever costs the opponent" was
    true for 40+ windows and false the turn its own Emrakul was out — the row printed `1 of
    yours` and the guide's unconditional sentence outranked it (`vs126` seq 44; `deck125/
    skill.md` S2, W21); deck123's RULE 5 said "N = 1 is the cast" beside "power 0 or 1 — not
    hurting you — keep the edict", and at `vs152` seq 6 they disagreed on a 1/1 Katilda whose
    card text makes her a lord — the pilot held, she was a 3/3 by turn 10 behind a Human board
    (`deck123/skill.md` S3, A50-10). Rule, extending #131's construction method from mulligan
    sections to RULE-level pairs and absolutes: for every "always"/"whatever"/"only ever"
    sentence and every pair of rules keyed to overlapping conditions, construct (a) the least
    harmful member of the class (a `[defender]`, a 0-power body, a token) and (b) the deck's own
    exception (its finisher creature, its token maker) and confirm ONE verdict; the exception is
    written INTO the sentence, keyed to the token that changes on the screen (`[defender]` on the
    victim's line, `1 of yours` on the sweeper row, the first card-text clause on a 1/1 lord).
    Companion render items (victim tags on the edict row; a converter tag on creature cast rows)
    are docketed (wave-51 D12, D13) so the key is on the row that asks.

136. A RENDER SHIP THAT ADDS A DECISION KIND IS PAIRED, THE SAME WAVE, WITH (a) A SECTION IN
    EVERY GUIDE NAMING THE ORDER FOR IT — COPIED FROM THE NEAREST EXISTING ORDER — AND (b) THE
    RETIREMENT OF EVERY GUIDE SENTENCE THAT DESCRIBED THE ENGINE BEHAVIOUR THE ASK REPLACED.
    Lane W's cleanup `discard` ask (28 records, a new kind) arrived with no guide text at any of
    seven seats. deck126 discarded the third Tribute over a Lantern on turn 4 (`vs123` seq 7)
    and died at -208 to the Bloodline Keeper that Tribute answers, while its bottoming order two
    sections down already said "Lantern or Staff first" (`deck126/skill.md` S2, F18); deck125
    sent a Cancel over a Lightmine Field at 44 life (`vs123` seq 76; `deck125/skill.md` S4,
    W25); deck123's A49-8 ("the engine — not you — chooses what you discard") was written for
    wave-49 H2 and its floor-shaped half failed 3/3 anyway while the pilot, once asked, chose
    sanely 7/7 (`deck123/skill.md` S4, A50-9). Rule: at each lane merge the reviewer's checklist
    carries two items — "which decision kinds are new this binary?" (each gets an ordered
    section derived from the closest existing one: bottoming -> discard; the London ask's shape
    -> any list-answer ask) and "which guide sentences describe an engine behaviour this lane
    changed?" (#128's grep finds them: "the engine discards" matched zero prompts this corpus).
    The rule that AVOIDED the window becomes the rule that ANSWERS it. This is the operational
    form of wave-49 boundary B1, which predicted exactly this pair of sentences going false.

137. NAMED-CARD CHECKS PORT ACROSS THE POOL'S GUIDES BY THEIR TAG STRING, AND WITHIN ONE GUIDE A
    CLASS EXCEPTION IS A CROSS-REFERENCE TO THE SECTION THAT ALREADY NAMES THE CARDS. deck123's
    CHECK 1 has priced Perimeter Captain / Pride Guardian since wave 45; deck130 met the same
    two walls at `130 vs126` seq 49 and handed over nine life with `(blocking trigger: they may
    gain 2)` printed on every attacker tag (`deck130/skill.md` S3, D50-7). In the same guide,
    deck123's RULE 3 "K of 0 — keep the sweeper" was written for two 0/4 walls; at `123 vs126`
    seq 17 the walls were the exact names CHECK 1 forbids attacking into, and the pilot broke
    the rule correctly (won -208) — the right key was already in another section (`deck123/
    skill.md` S5, A50-4). Rule: at Step 1 the reviewer lists the pool's named-card checks in the
    OTHER six guides and confirms each is present or inapplicable in this one — the tag string
    (`(blocking trigger: they may gain 2)`, `[defender]`, `[named: X]`) is identical at every
    seat, so the sentence ports verbatim; and where two sections of one guide name the same
    cards, the exception is written as a cross-reference ("K = 0 on Perimeter Captain or Pride
    Guardian: CHECK 1's walls — sweep them"), never as a new prose class. Extends #121's
    "soften an absolute with the row's count" and #81's coverage diff.

138. A RULE THAT FAILS IDENTICALLY IN A THIRD CORPUS WITH THE REPLY QUOTING THE GUIDE'S OWN
    ARITHMETIC OR ANTI-EXAMPLE ROUTES TO THE RENDER, AND THE GUIDE KEEPS ONE LINE. Two seats,
    same wave: Idyllic Tutor with an Alarm owned — wave 49 3 casts, wave 50 2 (`123 vs125` seq
    118, 139), the reply matching the guide's quoted anti-example each time, "Tutor: dead"
    written 0 times across both corpora (`deck123/skill.md` S6, A50-5; render M2); Hammer of
    Bogardan's return with the Commander in hand — wave 48, wave 49 x2, wave 50 (`130 vs123`
    seq 18, the plan saying "wait, I have 5 mana ... so I can cast it" and taking the return
    anyway) (`deck130/skill.md` S5, D50-1; render M3). The pattern: a rule keyed correctly to
    the screen, quoted back by the pilot, broken in the same reply — the executor is not
    failing to SEE, it is failing to SEQUENCE, and sequence is a render/protocol lever (the
    upkeep ask arrives before the main-phase menu exists; the Tutor row does not say what is
    already owned). Rule, the converse of #132 (which fires when the test cannot run): when a
    rule FAILS the same way in a third corpus and the reply quotes the rule, the seat file
    carries the render ask (wave-51 D8, D9) and the guide is left at ONE restatement — a fourth
    paragraph is the edit forbidden by #102's exhaustion clause.

139. THE #128 GREP IS RUN PER ROW FAMILY: FOR EVERY ANNOTATION A GUIDE RELIES ON, THE REVIEWER
    LISTS THE ROW FAMILIES THAT PRINT IT AND THE ONES THAT DO NOT, AND THE GUIDE NAMES THE
    SILENT FAMILY. Spell target menus print `{right now: takes N damage - DIES / SURVIVES
    (toughness T)}`; the activated-ability rows (`Deal 2 damage with Siege-Gang Commander
    targeting ...`, Spellbomb the same) printed nothing — 0 of 49 this corpus — and the pilot,
    trained by the spell rows to read a result, fired 2 at a 3/4 at 4 life and 2 at a walker at
    3 loyalty (`130 vs162` seq 23, 17; `deck130/skill.md` S1, D50-5; seat H2). Rule: an
    annotation the guide keys on is a fact about a row FAMILY, not about the game; where a
    sibling family lacks it the guide says so as a card fact ("these rows print no result — read
    the (P/T) or `[counters: N x loyalty]` yourself: 2 damage does not kill a 3/4") until the
    render half ships (wave-51 D6). The #103 grep of a quoted literal is the special case of
    this check.

140. A TWO-SCREEN COMMIT IS TAUGHT WITH ITS EXIT ONE SCREEN EARLIER, AND THE EXIT ROW IS QUOTED.
    The X menu after `Cast Card Normally` spends the card on every row; deck130's (a)/(b) rules
    were obeyed at the cast row five times in one game and broken at the X menu once the pilot
    had committed (`130 vs126` seq 60: "without killing Siege-Gang Commander" written beside
    `X=3 kills THEIRS: Pride Guardian; YOURS: Siege-Gang Commander`, the Commander died for a
    0/3); the `Choose an option` menu's `Decline - do nothing` row was never quoted in the guide
    (`deck130/skill.md` S2, D50-4/D50-8). Rule: for any commit that spans screens (cast row ->
    option menu -> X menu; Tutor -> reveal list; a `PUT:` ask after a keep), the guide states
    the LAST screen on which "cast nothing" is still an answer, quotes that row's literal, and
    says the screens after it have none. The render-side exit row on the X menu is docketed with
    the engine seat's ruling pending (wave-51 D25); the guide sentence is true either way.

141. A DAMAGE-PREVENTION RULE NAMES THE QUANTITY IT GOVERNS AND THE SIBLING QUANTITY IT DOES
    NOT, AND THE KILL CASE CARRIES ITS OWN CONDITION. deck130's anti-triple-block rule (wave 48,
    "one blocker stops one attacker's damage") was read at `130 vs162` seq 22 as a ban on the
    kill the header priced (`GANG BLOCK: your 3 biggest together deal 4, enough to kill this
    attacker`) — at 7 life against a draw punisher, the turn before the draw step killed the
    seat (`deck130/skill.md` S4, D50-6). Rule, extending #122's "state the post-action
    quantity": a rule about damage says "damage", says that a kill the header prices is a
    different question, and writes the kill case with its condition — the attacker's identity
    (a name on the `DRAW PUNISHERS` line; the only clock) and the life after its `deals N`.
    The render companion (the GANG clause naming the punisher) is wave-51 D24.

142. A FIXED-NUMBER GATE THAT FAILS FOR SEVEN CORPORA WHILE ITS BREAKS STOP COSTING GAMES IS
    RE-DERIVED FROM ITS PURPOSE, NOT RESTATED — THE NUMBER WAS ONE CASE'S CONSTANT. deck125's
    Staff gate ("leaves 5 or more") failed 3/6 then 2/5 casts across two corpora; this corpus
    both breaks were harmless BY THE GATE'S OWN PURPOSE (`vs162` seq 20: the only counter in
    hand was an Essence Scatter against a deck that cast no creature; `vs123` seq 29: leaves 2
    with a 2-mana Scatter). The "5" was Fall of the Gavel's cost generalised to every counter
    (`deck125/skill.md` S1, W22). Rule, what to do at #102's exhaustion besides routing to the
    engine: when a numeric gate's breaks stop correlating with losses, ask whether the number
    was one case's constant; if so, write the gate as the QUANTITY it stands for, read off a
    printed surface (the cost of the cheapest counter in hand that can hit what the opponent
    casts — the hand line prints `Essence Scatter {1}{u}`), and keep the old losses as the test
    that the new rule still forbids them (the wave-49 `vs152` taps-out-with-a-Scatter loss stays
    illegal). #118's "shrink, re-key" applied to a number instead of a key.

143. A LIST-ANSWER ASK (`PUT: n, m`) IS A THIRD EMIT SURFACE WITH THE SAME FAILURE MODE AS THE
    CHOICE AND PLAN LINES, AND THE GUIDE STATES THE LIST'S CONTENT RULE IN EMIT FORM PLUS THE
    ONE CLASS THAT NEVER ENTERS IT AT THE CURRENT N. `146 vs126` seq 4: the bottom ask at
    (keeping 5) on a 2-land keep; the reply's PLAN said "play Shineshadow Snarl and Brightclimb
    Pathway" and its PUT line sent the Pathway under — two lands from turn 3 to turn 14, 0/35
    (`deck146/skill.md` S-1, 146-H). The guide's rule was a board predicate the executor had to
    evaluate; the reply evaluated it correctly and emitted the wrong numbers. #105 (shape with
    blanks) and #120 (gate first) were written for CHOICE/PLAN. Rule: where an ask's answer is
    a list of card numbers (bottoming, the cleanup `discard`, annihilator picks), the guide
    states the content rule as the list would be written ("the numbers of the highest-cost
    spells, most expensive first") and the one class that never enters it at the current N
    ("no land from a keep of two or fewer"), and tells the pilot to read the list back against
    its own plan sentence. Metric: PUT lines containing a card the same reply's PLAN names as a
    play (0/N).

144. CROSS-GUIDE CONVERGENCE IS A CHECKLIST ITEM: WHEN ONE GUIDE RE-KEYS A RULE TO A RENDERED
    LITERAL, THE BOUNDARY PASS GREPS EVERY OTHER GUIDE'S SAME SECTION FOR THE PRE-KEY FORM AND
    LISTS THE HOLDOUTS BY NAME — THE DIFF IS BETWEEN KEYS, NOT ONLY BETWEEN VERDICTS. deck152's
    RULE -1 line ("one land under `would not cover any spell in it` ships") was written in wave
    48 after a 33-turn no-cast loss; deck146's STEP 2 still said "one land when the spells cost
    3 or more ... judgment call" and kept exactly that six (`146 vs125` seq 2, no second land
    until turn 19, -12/21; `deck146/skill.md` S-2, 146-G). #81's coverage-diff obligation fired
    in wave 49's boundary pass for the mulligan FLOOR text but not for the coverage-line KEY.
    Rule: the boundary report carries, per re-key, the other guides' same-section sentences
    that still carry the pre-key form; a holdout is a finding whether or not it has failed yet.

145. EVERY CLASS WORD IN A GUIDE CONDITION (CREATURE, PLANESWALKER, NONLAND, PERMANENT) IS
    GREPPED IN THE PRIMITIVE'S TARGET/FILTER CLAUSE, AND WHERE ORACLE AND PRIMITIVE DISAGREE THE
    GUIDE STATES THE CARD FACT THE ENGINE ACTUALLY DELIVERS WHILE THE SEAT ROUTES THE SCRIPT FIX.
    deck146's entry 1 said "creature or planeswalker you can hit" for Soul Shatter; the
    primitive (`borderline.txt:106093`) filters `creature[manacost=convertedcost:highest:*:
    myBattlefield]` — creature-only, ranked over every permanent — and the seat planned Soul
    Shatter "for Ob Nixilis" twice (`146 vs162` seq 21, 25) and then lost the game to the
    no-sacrifice defect that ranking produces (`deck146/skill.md` S-3; seat E-1; wave-51 D1,
    IN FLIGHT). Rule: the brief's card-fact step (read the primitive) gains a mechanical half —
    each class word in a condition is checked against the primitive's filter. Where they
    disagree, the divergence is a CARD-SCRIPT defect (owner rule: express the Oracle faithfully
    in script; the /wagic-cardscript loop owns it) and is docketed; meanwhile the guide's
    condition is keyed to the class the engine will act on, written as a card fact ("Soul
    Shatter takes their highest-MV creature"), never as a description of the divergence (#99/
    #103) — and the reviewer re-keys to the Oracle class the wave the fix ships (#136's checklist
    item catches it).

146. A MATCHUP RULE'S IMPERATIVES ARE AUDITED AGAINST WHAT THE PRINTED ROW SAYS THE ACTION
    DOES ON THAT BOARD — A RULE WHOSE ACTION THE ROW PRICES AS FATAL IS A FALSE SENTENCE
    HOWEVER SAFE IT SOUNDS. deck146's both-halves bullet said "block every [lifelink] attacker";
    the A-row printed `... chains without limit - fatal to you, not a trade`; the pilot wrote
    "there is no loop", blocked, 11 -> 0 (`146 vs126` seq 49; `deck146/skill.md` S-4, 146-L).
    Lifelink pays on damage to a blocker; the chain runs either way. #114 says write the
    mechanism; this is #114's audit form for EXISTING text: for each imperative in a matchup
    rule, find the row the action lands on and read its parenthesis — where the row prices the
    action as fatal, the sentence is cut, not softened. The ATTACK half of the same bullet held
    4/4 (`ATTACK: none` on every priced window) — the audit is per imperative, not per rule.

147. EVERY PERMANENT WITH AN ACTIVATED ABILITY THE EMITTER CAN OFFER IN UPKEEP GETS A SECTION
    BEFORE ITS FIRST CORPUS, KEYED TO THE ROW'S PRESENT FORMS. #129 was written after deck130's
    Hammer and deck146's Hive had each cost a game; deck152's Lair of the Hydra had no section
    at all and was offered 34 times this corpus — taken on a `[this land is TAPPED ...]` row
    twice (`152 vs125` seq 16, `152 vs126` seq 24) and on a `[repeat: activated this turn 1
    times already]` row twice (`152 vs125` seq 59, 73) (`deck152/skill.md` S-1, 152-E). The
    engine's tags were complete; the guide had nothing to key them to. Rule, extending #129 and
    #111: the Step-1 deck read lists every permanent whose activated ability can appear in an
    Upkeep window (animating lands, pumps, returns), and each gets at least a two-line entry
    keyed to the row's tags (`[this land is TAPPED ...]`, `[repeat: ...]`, `{paying this taps:
    ...}`) BEFORE the first corpus, not after the first loss. Metric (#117): offers by phase
    and takes on tagged rows, per sink. The Upkeep-only offer skew (Hive 11/11 in Upkeep) is an
    engine item (wave-51 D7), not a fourth restatement.

148. A PER-CARD EXCEPTION TO THE BLOCK LADDER IS KEYED TO THE B-ROW PARENTHESIS AND THE HEADER
    N, NEVER TO THE ATTACKER'S IDENTITY. deck152's "never swap Katilda with a 1/1 mana creature"
    was keyed to the wave-46 story; the failing windows were a 1/1 Goblin TOKEN (`152 vs146`
    seq 22, 17 life) and a 3/3 Human token (`152 vs123` seq 19, 20 life) — the identity clause
    matched neither in the pilot's reading, and both replies argued the block "saves life"
    (`deck152/skill.md` S-2, 152-F). #126 (re-key to the printed string) applies; the addition
    is the pairing with the ladder's own number: "Katilda's B-row + `(both die)` or `(your
    blocker dies)` + `you would be at N` >= 10 -> not assigned", so the exception is evaluated
    by the same read the ladder already demands.

149. BEFORE A VIOLATED-UNPUNISHED VERDICT IS CARRIED TO #118'S CEILING, THE WINNING GAME'S
    EVENTS ARE READ FOR THE DAMAGE SOURCE — IF THE "VIOLATION" IS WHAT DEALT THE DAMAGE, THE
    RULE'S COUNT IS MISSING A CONVERTER AND THE FIX IS A FACT. deck162's RULE 2 counted
    punishers (draw -> damage) and braked draw engines at zero; Liliana's Caress converts
    DISCARDS, which the same engines cause once the hand is full, and the seat's `vs123` win
    ran 14 damage through Caress before any punisher landed (events at seq 9/11/16). Four
    corpora scored those engine casts as "violated-unpunished" (#64/#118) when three of the
    five were the deck's actual kill (`deck162/skill.md` S-1, 162-E). Rule, a #106 companion:
    a brake keyed to a count must count every converter of the resource it brakes, and the
    missing converter is found by reading the WIN's narration, not the loss's. The engine-side
    count (wave-49 D15, carried as wave-51 D11) gains the same converter.

150. THE LETHAL CHECK ENUMERATES THE ONE-SHOT SOURCES THE PILOT CONTROLS, NOT ONLY THE PER-TURN
    ONES, EACH WITH ITS TIMING WINDOW. deck162's LETHAL CHECK multiplied Mines and Boxes by P
    and never priced Ob Nixilis's -2 ("its controller draws two cards" = 2 x P at once); the
    seat passed a lethal -2 twice at their 3 life (`162 vs126` seq 23/24; `deck162/skill.md`
    S-2, 162-D). #112 put the lethal count first in the turn for a creature-mana deck; this is
    the same audit for a punisher deck: every card whose text makes the OPPONENT draw (Ob
    Nixilis -2, Peer into the Abyss, Forced Fruition on their cast) gets a line in the
    arithmetic with its window (sorcery speed; on their cast). Render companion: the row
    carries the arithmetic (wave-51 D14).

151. "DO NOT GO OUTSIDE THIS LIST" NAMES THE LIST IT MEANS — THE MENU — AND EVERY GUIDE CARRIES
    ONE SENTENCE TYING THE CHOICE TO A PRINTED ROW WITH THE COMMONEST REASON A HAND CARD HAS
    NONE. All three of the corpus's fallbacks: `CHOICE: 1 (Cast Sanguine Bond)` / `(Cast
    Exquisite Blood)` naming a card in the HAND whose pips the untapped lands could not pay
    (`126 vs125` seq 14 with `{B} 1` on the mana line; `vs162` seq 16; `vs130` seq 13), each
    classified `stale_echo`, Baka then casting row 1 in two of the three (`deck126/skill.md`
    S3, F19; seat-125-126 HIGH #1; engine seat D-4). Rule 7's "do not go outside this list"
    was about the guide's ENTRY list. Rule: one sentence per guide — "a CHOICE names a numbered
    row on THIS window; a card on your hand line with no `Cast` row is there because a pip
    cannot be paid — read the mana line's per-colour count" — keyed to the mana line. The
    engine half (a `[RE-ASK]` that prints the mismatch instead of a fallback) is wave-51 D3.

**Supporting instances recorded, not amended.** deck125 W20/S3: a rule restated in the model's
own plan line and broken in the same reply (`vs126` seq 42, Emrakul into Exquisite Blood) —
#102/#132's exhaustion shape; re-keyed to the printed `{effect:}` text, render half D13.
deck126 S4: the header-keyed "of which 1 is a creature" re-keyed to `<name> is sacrificed, you
gain N` the moment the row carried it — #118 applied. deck152 S-3 and the engine seat's five
`answer_replaced` audits: every last-clean-line execution this corpus was a correct
self-revision (`152 vs126` seq 40 lethal; `146 vs126` seq 18 `A1, A2` -> `none`) — #116 holds,
no change. deck162 S-3: the wave-49 boundary pass's all-lands sentence added (162-F) with the
twelve-hand check re-run — #131 working. deck146's Hive takes in Upkeep (`146 vs126` seq 31/35,
8 mana burned, `ATTACK: none` after): #109's "read the alternative" fired the wrong way once the
alternative was `pass`; the lever is the offer's PHASE (engine D7), not a restatement.
deck125's seven Elixir/Staff-class breaks under the fixed-5 gate: subsumed by #142. The
`x1` repeat takes (`123 vs130` seq 30, 31): harmless singles, no rule.


=====================================================================
EDITION AMENDMENTS — wave-51 (2026-08-27) — amendments 152-167
=====================================================================
Lessons from the wave-51 corpus review (eighth fair-hand corpus, `matchups-20260827-155545`,
binary master c010ddb47 = lanes A/B/C/D/E/F + the Vita oracle fixes; **42/42 seats carry a
`gameend`, 21/21 natural, 2,129 decisions, 5 fallbacks = 0.23% — `named_row_reask` 3 (all
recovered), `unparsed_reply` 1, `stale_livelock` 1 (NEW class); Baka-executed 2** — verified on
disk by this step; the "deck123-vs-deck162 dead-loop, excluded" note carried by one seat file
describes an older run and is dropped for the THIRD wave running). Each rule traces to a cited
seat finding. Standing owner doctrine (2026-08-26) governs every rule below: the REVIEWER owns
the deck guide, synthesis owns this skill and the general strategy, the core loop is the
purpose; hard caps on the model's legal choices are rejected; every guide rule is reasoned and
odds-based, never a code-like floor. This wave's through-line: **the six lanes shipped clean by
string (Soul Shatter 15/15 with two walkers, the planner 1/421, the re-ask 3/3 recovered, the
receipt 53/53, the tags on 100% of their rows) and the losses moved to three places the skill
had not looked: the ENGINE ACTING BETWEEN THE MODEL'S ANSWERS (a repeat loop handed to Baka, a
PUT executed as a different row, a planner tapping three walls for one), a PRINTED COUNT OR TAG
READ WITHOUT ITS EXCEPTION (the `{feeds:}` K, the `[already owned:` tag, the `[from exile]`
tag, the SURVIVES row), and a MULLIGAN CLAUSE CARRIED PAST ITS LOOK (a two-card keep).**

152. EVERY LIST-ANSWER ASK IS SCORED reply-numbers == `chosen_text` BEFORE ANY PLAN IS READ, AND
    THE #143 PUT-vs-PLAN METRIC COUNTS ONLY CARDS THE PLAN NAMES AS AN ACTION. `162 vs146` s17:
    reply `PUT: 3 (Forced Fruition)`, printed row 3 = Forced Fruition, executed = Liliana's
    Caress (row 2; `chosen_text` and the narration agree) — the deck's only discard converter
    binned on the engine's read, not the pilot's (`deck146/skill.md` S-3, `deck162/skill.md`
    S-2, seat-146 E-1). #143 as written scores the pilot's list against its plan and would have
    PASSED this window. Rule (a): the reviewer's FIRST check at every `PUT:` / `BLOCKS:` /
    `ATTACK:` list is the reply's numbers against the log's executed names; 0 mismatches is the
    pass, and a mismatch is an ENGINE item before any guide sentence is touched (wave-52 docket
    D3). Rule (b), the class word #143 lacked (`deck125/skill.md` S4): 3/15 PUT lines at deck125
    named a card the PLAN mentioned, but two mentioned it as a RULE ("do not cast Supreme Verdict
    unless ...") — the metric counts a PUT card the PLAN names as a PLAY (cast / play / activate)
    and the reviewer reports both numbers (letter 3/15, intent 1/15).

153. A MULLIGAN SECTION NAMES ONE PROPERTY THE PILOT MAY SHIP ON — THE ENGINE'S LAND COUNT AND
    COVERAGE LINE — AND STATES EVERY OTHER PROPERTY AS A BOTTOM-ASK QUESTION; THE #131 CHECK GAINS
    A CARRY STEP AND A THIRTEENTH HAND. `146 vs125` s1-s6: deck146's STEP 2 carried "or NO source
    of one of your colors when the header shows every spell needs it" — look-scoped in the text,
    unscoped in the pilot's reading: the clause became the PLAN at look one ("find a hand with at
    least one white mana source"), was quoted by name at look two, and the CARRIED plan then
    shipped (keeping 5) [3 lands, covering two spells], (keeping 4) and (keeping 3) against STEP
    1's own "keep with even one land" — a two-card keep, first spell turn 11, -14/45 at T80
    (`deck146/skill.md` S-1; seat-123-130's ruling deleting the clause, 9-of-21 odds; seat-146's
    146-M). #131's per-look construction agreed with the clause at every look because the failure
    was the CARRY, not the look. Rule: (a) one shippable property per section (deck152's "Not a
    colour, not a two-drop, not a curve: those are bottom-ask questions" + its "THE CARRIED PLAN IS
    NOT EVIDENCE ABOUT THIS HAND" paragraph are the form; #144's cross-guide grep finds the
    holdouts); (b) where a guide keeps any second shippable property, #131 is extended by one
    step — write the look-N PLAN the clause would produce and check that plan against the look-N+1
    hand; (c) the twelve hands gain a thirteenth, "2 lands / no coverage" at (keeping 7) and
    (keeping 6) — the shape a two-colour deck deals most often (`deck126/skill.md` S4: the seat
    improvised it correctly; F24 wrote it in odds form). Odds, never a floor: the ruling's form
    is "nine of your 21 lands make W; the second colour is a draw away; a ship costs a card for
    the same land odds".

154. A LANE THAT ADDS A TAG TO — OR COMPLETES — A ROW FAMILY A GUIDE RULES ON IS A MANDATORY
    RE-KEY IN THE SAME WAVE'S REVISION, BEFORE THE CORPUS; THE #139 TABLE IS RE-RUN PER CORPUS FOR
    EVERY FAMILY A LANE TOUCHED, AND IT GAINS A TAG-COVERAGE COLUMN. Three seats, one law:
    deck130's D50-5 taught "ability rows print NO result" one wave ago and lane E printed the
    result 428 times at that seat — the sentence was false on every window of the corpus and
    stayed until the revision (`deck130/skill.md` S1); wave-50 boundary B5 said "re-key the Lair
    sentence to D7's annotation when it lands", lane E shipped `[Upkeep offer: ...]`, the sentence
    still said "MAIN 1 only" in prose, and the first Upkeep take under the tag happened (`152
    vs125` s36; `deck152/skill.md` S-3); `[from exile]` had no word in deck123's guide and the
    pilot narrated it FALSELY 0-of-4 ("Intruder Alarm is exiled, I cannot cast it" under a `Cast
    Intruder Alarm {4}{u} [from exile]` row, `123 vs152` s20/24/26/27; `deck123/skill.md` S1).
    Rule: #136's checklist ("which guide sentences describe an engine behaviour this lane
    changed?") gains "which guide sentences will a NEW tag key better than their current
    words?" — the tag is on the row before the reviewer sees the corpus, so the re-key is due at
    revision time; #139's per-family table gains a third column — for every bracket tag the
    emitter can print on a row family the guide's cards appear in, the guide names the tag ONCE
    with its meaning; a tag the pilot narrates falsely in its first corpus is a FIRST-failure
    prose fix, not a third-failure shrink.

155. A GATE THAT COMPARES TWO PRINTED NUMBERS AND FAILS THE PLAN-TEXT METRIC MOVES ONTO THE ROW
    VIA THE CLAUSE THE EMITTER ALREADY PRINTS ON THE SIBLING ROW FAMILY; A HIDDEN COST IS KEYED TO
    THE STRING THAT REVEALS WHICH SOURCE PAYS, NEVER TO A LIFE NUMBER. deck125's tap-out gate
    (row `leaves N` vs a hand counter's cost) was in the plan line of BOTH breaking replies
    (`vs152` s24, `vs162` s24; `plan_echo_count` 5/4) and the Staff was cast at `leaves 1` with a
    3-cost counter in hand anyway — #102's exhaustion on a MANA gate; lane E already prints
    `{spends K of your M untapped mana sources this turn; <card> in your hand needs K}` on ABILITY
    rows (`vs130` s8) (`deck125/skill.md` S1, G1). deck130's "life 3 or less" Talisman floor
    failed three times in ONE game (`130 vs126` s49 3->2, s82 2->1, s85 1->0, gameend 0/24 with the
    opponent never attacking) because the plan never priced the Talisman; the row's own `{leaves
    0 of your 1}` plus the `Those sources` line is the trigger a pilot can see
    (`deck130/skill.md` S3). Rule: when a guide gate is a comparison of two printed numbers and
    its plan-text metric fails, the remedy is the SAME clause the engine emits on the sibling
    family — the reviewer names the existing clause and the row family that lacks it (docket
    D17/D7), the guide keeps one line; any hidden cost (pain lands, Talismans, phyrexian mana) is
    taught at the string that reveals the paying source, with a dictated "pays: life L -> L-1".

156. A PRINTED COUNT IS THE STRONGEST KEY ON THE SCREEN: A RULE KEYED TO IT CARRIES ITS
    EXCEPTIONS IN THE SAME SENTENCE, AND A CONVERTER THE GUIDE QUALIFIES IS RE-QUALIFIED BESIDE THE
    STRING, NEVER BY A SECOND COUNT. Lane F put `converters on your battlefield: K` on every
    engine row; deck162's brake said "count the names on your battlefield line" and its one
    exemption (the FIRST Howling Mine) lived in cast-order entry 5. The pilot read the new "0"
    as the brake in FOUR windows with no Mine out (`162 vs130` s5/6/9/10, the over-brake) and
    read past it once WITH a Mine out (`162 vs146` s6, the break, plan "stack Mines once a
    punisher is out" written while doing it) (`deck162/skill.md` S-1; 162-G). Corollary for #149:
    the engine's K counts Liliana's Caress unconditionally; the hand-size qualifier is written
    beside the K sentence ("when the only name after K is Caress, K counts only while their hand
    line reads 7 or more"), not as a rival count. Render companion: the Caress-only K carries the
    hand size (wave-52 docket, LOW).

157. #118'S CEILING HAS A RE-DERIVATION FORM: WHEN EVERY BREAK OF A VIOLATED-UNPUNISHED RULE
    SHARES A PRINTED FACT THE RULE DID NOT NAME, THAT FACT IS THE RULE'S MISSING CONDITION AND
    THE COUNT RESETS; A TIMING RULE WRITTEN FROM ONE CATASTROPHE NAMES THE CARD CLASS THAT MADE
    IT ONE. deck126's Lantern-over-wall: 2 + 4 + 1+1 + 2 breaks across four corpora, every one
    with a five-mana enchantment (or Tutor) on the hand line at <= 4 sources, every game won —
    the rule was written from "a wall is a body"; the breaks were the model reading the hand
    (`deck126/skill.md` S1; F21). deck123's "YOUR OWN UPKEEP IS THE WORST WINDOW OF ALL" was true
    against the wave-44 sweeper and false in 4 of 4 own-turn chains since (all won at the
    L + C + 3 stop) — re-conditioned on the opponent's log showing Starstorm / Supreme Verdict /
    Damnation (`deck123/skill.md` S3; A51-13). deck130's "Blastminer alone: ATTACK: none — always"
    forfeited seven damage into an empty board at 0 opposing nonbasics (`deck130/skill.md` S4;
    D51-6) — #135's absolute-about-a-class, confirmed: a role rule for a utility creature states
    the JOB it is kept for, so the pilot can see when the job is gone. Rule: before restating a
    violated-unpunished rule, list the breaking windows' shared printed fact (hand line, mana
    line, opponent log); if every break shares one the rule did not name, the rule gains that
    condition (re-key, not restate). Companion to #149 (read the WIN).

158. AT A SECOND IDENTICAL FAILURE WHERE THE PLAN QUOTES THE MECHANISM, THE REVIEWER READS THE
    PARAGRAPH AFTER THE RULE FOR AN IMPERATIVE THAT OUTRANKS IT IN THE PILOT'S READING ORDER —
    THE FIX IS ORDER, NOT TEXT. `130 vs126` s20 (19 life): all four attacker tags read `(neither
    dies (blocking trigger: they may gain 2, and if they do their converter takes 2 off you))`,
    the PLAN explained the mechanism correctly and sent all four (19 -> 11, 16 -> 24); s28 the
    same with three Goblins (10 -> 4). Same matchup, same shape as wave 50 — #132's paired-edit
    replay FAILED. #102(b) said look for a contradiction elsewhere; it was ADJACENT: the ATTACK
    FLOOR's "send EVERY creature listed" sat one paragraph below the WALL CHECK, and the executor
    ran the floor (`deck130/skill.md` S2; D51-1 made the wall check the floor's FIRST case).
    Rule: #102's second-failure step is a read of the NEXT paragraph for an outranking
    imperative; when found, the fix is to make the check the first case of the imperative it
    lost to, with the arithmetic in emit form ("Wall: <n> attackers x 2 = <2n> life; ATTACK:
    none").

159. THE #151 SENTENCE CARRIES BOTH HALVES: A HAND CARD WITH NO `Cast` ROW IS NOT CASTABLE, AND
    A PRINTED ROW IS PAYABLE. `126 vs162` s17 (13 life): Tribute on a Fog Bank taken over a
    printed `2. Cast Sanguine Bond {3}{b}{b} {leaves 0 ...}` row with the reply "we still lack the
    two black mana for Sanguine Bond" — the mirror of F19's lesson, a printed row believed
    unpayable (`deck126/skill.md` S2; F22). Rule: the one #151 sentence per guide reads "the
    engine prints a row for every spell you can pay for right now — a printed row is payable, a
    hand card without one is not"; and #102's plan-text form applies to the false premise beside
    it ("IF YOUR PLAN SAYS remove their blocker, THE PLAN IS ALREADY WRONG: nothing of yours
    attacks").

160. A "WHICH HALF DO I HAVE" PICK IS KEYED TO BOTH LINES THAT PRINT OWNERSHIP, IN THE ORDER THE
    PROMPT PRINTS THEM. `126 vs146` s28-29: Sanguine Bond on the battlefield line, Exquisite
    Blood on the hand line WITH a `Cast` row on the same menu — the reply cast the Tutor ("Find
    Sanguine Bond") and `PUT: 15` = a second Bond; the win waited from t18 to t22
    (`deck126/skill.md` S3; F23). Rule: any rule of the form "take the one you do not have" reads
    the battlefield line AND the hand line before the PUT line, and "a missing name that is on
    your HAND line with a `Cast` row is entry 1, not the Tutor"; the reviewer's #128 grep covers
    the phrase "already have".

161. AN EXCEPTION THAT NARROWS A SAFETY GATE BY OPPONENT BEHAVIOUR ("ONLY WHEN THEY HAVE SHOWN
    X") IS CHECKED AGAINST EVERY POOL DECK'S PRIMITIVE LIST FOR X BEFORE IT SHIPS; IF ANY POOL
    DECK RUNS X, IT DOES NOT SHIP. deck125's W22 ("a Scatter counts only when the opponent's line
    or log shows creatures") was derived from one wave-50 break that cost nothing; deck162 runs
    Master of the Feast (5/5 flying) and Fate Unraveler, and the seat tapped out on turn 7
    against a line showing only Howling Mine + Liliana's Caress — the Master resolved on turn 8
    with no window and took the seat from 21 to 1 (`deck125/skill.md` S2; `vs162` s10-13; W27
    reverted it). #145's grep, applied to the OPPONENT side: the exception's class word is
    checked against the pool, not against the one log that suggested it.

162. A RULE FIXING THE SIZE OF A SCALABLE EFFECT STATES THE ONE BOARD ON WHICH THE SIZE IS THE
    LARGEST OFFERED, KEYED TO THE HEADER NUMBER. deck125's "X is always 3" was written from
    discard-pile evidence and had no branch for the turn the spell IS the seat's life: `vs152`
    s39 (1 life, a 3/1 lifelink on their line, `max affordable X=7` on the menu) cast a second
    Staff and died to the 3/1 (`deck125/skill.md` S3; W30). Rule: every size rule for an X spell,
    a pump, a Revelation carries its life-critical branch ("your life is 5 or less and the
    opponent header's second number is 1 or more -> the LARGEST X offered"), keyed to the printed
    life and the header count, never to "when desperate" (#72c).

163. A PER-CARD EXCEPTION IS WRITTEN FOR BOTH SIDES OF COMBAT AT ONCE. #148 keyed Katilda's
    B-row to the parenthesis and the header N; her A-row twin was left to the generic stop rule,
    and the next corpus broke it on exactly that card (`152 vs146` s12: a 1/1 mana engine sent
    into `(your attacker dies, their blocker lives)` on turn 6; she died, the second Katilda was
    edicted, 20 -> 3 by T10) (`deck152/skill.md` S-1; 152-G). Rule: a creature the guide singles
    out on defence is singled out on offence in the same paragraph — the parenthesis strings are
    one family (`your attacker dies` / `your blocker dies`), so the second sentence costs one
    line.

164. "THE ONLY ANSWER", "REMOVAL", "THE ONLY WAY" ARE CARD-FACT CLAIMS AND GET #145'S GREP FOR A
    RETURN PATH. deck152's Spellbinder bullet called its exile "the ONLY answer this deck has to
    an enchantment"; the primitive's `canplayfromexile` + `changecost(colorless:2)` (Oracle: "its
    owner may play it ... costs {2} more") makes it a TAX, and `152 vs126` s49 shows the exiled
    Bond cast from exile into the loop that won (`deck152/skill.md` S-2; 152-H). Rule: any guide
    sentence that calls a card an answer is checked against the primitive's `moveto` /
    `canplayfromexile` / `transforms` clause for a return path and written as the effect the
