    engine delivers ("buys turns; the card comes back for {2} more"). Extends #145 from class
    words to effect words.

165. AN ABSOLUTE KEYED TO A PRINTED TAG GOES INSIDE THE NUMBERED PROCEDURE AS ITS FIRST STEP,
    NEVER BESIDE IT. deck146's Hive section has CHECK 0-3 as a numbered list and the `[repeat:
    ...]` sentence as a separate paragraph ("read it before you read anything else"); three
    replies (`146 vs125` s91, s112, s262) ran CHECK 0, 1, 2, 3 in writing and never mentioned the
    tag on the row they took — twelve mana for three 3/3s that already existed
    (`deck146/skill.md` S-2). The executor runs the list; prose beside the list is not in the
    sequence (#133/#138). Rule: "CHECK -1: the row prints `[repeat:` -> PASS, stop" is the first
    numbered step. Left unapplied to deck146 this wave — #138 routes a third-corpus identical
    failure to the render (docket D12) and forbids the fourth restatement; the rule is for the
    next guide that adds a check list.

166. A MANA SOURCE THAT IS NOT MANA UNTIL ACTIVATED IS TAUGHT AS A COST, NOT A CHOICE: THE
    PROMPT'S OWN COUNT FIRST, THE FIRST WINDOW SECOND, THE COLOUR THIRD. `123 vs130` s6-s13: `Put
    a card onto the battlefield with Marsh Flats` passed SIX windows (turns 5-11) with the PLAN
    reading "Cast Thraben Doomsayer next turn when I have 3 mana" — the third source WAS the
    Flats, and the prompt's `Mana available: 2` said so every window; both Scrublands were
    destroyed by t11 and the seat died at -2 with no token (`deck123/skill.md` S2; A51-1). The
    guide had framed the fetch as "WHICH dual" (a choice) while the pilot counted the Flats as a
    land it already had. Rule: for fetch lands, Treasure, and rocks whose mana the engine offers
    as a priority row, the guide's first sentence is the prompt's own count ("Mana available does
    not count it"), the second is "the first window it is listed — on either player's turn", and
    the colour choice comes third. Render companion: the fetch row says the land makes no mana
    (docket D16).

167. A ROTATION CALL IS MADE ON OPEN GUIDE LANES, NOT ON THE RECORD, AND THE SEAT FILE LISTS
    PER LOSS "WINDOW / NO WINDOW". deck162's 2-4: three of the four losses had no window in the
    log with a better legal answer (a 21-creature Alarm board on turn 11; a four-land turn-8 first
    spell; Starstorm + Rorix); the one with a window is the one edited (`deck162/skill.md` S-3).
    deck146's 3-3 is a mulligan chain, a land-destruction draw and a loop; deck125's 2-4 has two
    no-lever losses (seat-125-126 "Rotation evidence"). The new-baseline rule (hands are real)
    already says this for win rates; it governs the rotation call too — a deck stays on the
    roster for its open lanes and exits when they close, whatever its n=6 record.

**Supporting instances recorded, not amended.** deck123 S4 (Tutor with an Alarm owned, the
dictated "Tutor: dead" sentence written verbatim and the Tutor cast in the same reply, `123 vs125`
s105; fourth corpus): #138 holds — the guide stays at one restatement, the residual is the render
(D10's wrong-half tag) and the parser (D6's index-name conflict at s48). deck123 S5 (deck130's
GANG-BLOCK rule ported to deck123 by its tag string, A51-10): #137/#144 applied, no change.
deck130 S5 (the deck126 loss shape identical in two consecutive corpora, #132 replay FAIL): the
guide half is at its second restatement (D51-1/D51-4) and #158 names the mechanism; the third
corpus decides the row-annotation route. deck146's Lolth 0 at 3 and 2 life with the reply saying
"we must pass" (`146 vs125` s282): the #133 reversed-decision shape in natural language — the
lever is lane C's conflict pattern (docket D14), no restatement. deck152's two-land ships under
"would not cover" (`152 vs125` s2, `146 vs162` s1): judgment calls neither guide has a sentence
for — #153(c)'s thirteenth hand is the reviewer's to write in odds form. The `x1` and single-row
"pass"-under-CHOICE takes (`123 vs162` s29, `123 vs126` s37/s44, `123 vs125` s15): harmless
singles; the parser scope is docket D14. deck125's `vs126` s17 Verdict declined at `2 without a
restriction` (two 1/1 lifelink Vampires): first instance, unpunished, recorded (#64/#118).


=====================================================================
EDITION AMENDMENTS — wave-52 (2026-09-02) — amendments 168-186
=====================================================================
Lessons from the wave-52 corpus review (NINTH fair-hand corpus, `matchups-20260901-223430`,
binary master dddb6f62b = lanes G/H/I/J/K/L + the owner batches + the option-preserving autotap
+ the Baka pump-targeting fix; pilot `qwen36-35b-a3b` FP8 on Spark :8084 — the 122B is retired).
**42/42 seats carry a `gameend`, 21/21 natural, 3,384 records / 3,300 decisions (wave 51: 2,129),
15 fallbacks = 0.45% — `plan_choice_conflict` 5, `empty_reply` 3, `unparsed_reply` 3,
`multiblock_reask` 3, `named_row_reask` 1; Baka-executed 6 = 0.18%** — every count re-derived on
disk by this step. Each rule below traces to a cited seat finding. Standing owner doctrine
(2026-08-26) governs: the REVIEWER owns the deck guide, synthesis owns this skill and the general
strategy, the core loop — engine correctness, LLM UX, bugs — is the purpose; hard caps on the
model's legal choices are rejected on sight; every guide rule is reasoned and odds-based.

This wave's through-line: **six lanes shipped and the whole render vocabulary the guides were
keyed to CHANGED UNDER THEM in one wave.** `[already owned:` went to 0 renders and split into
`[legendary:` / `[second copy:` / `[finds only ...]`; the bare `[from exile]` gained a 20-word
clause; `-N/-N` target rows gained DIES/SURVIVES; opponent-turn casting windows went from 0 to
884. Two guides' rules went from N/N to 0/N without a word of their text changing (deck126's
Lantern rule 9/9 declines -> 5/5 takes; deck123's "the Slip's rows print no verdict" sentence
became false), and the two guides that were re-keyed in the same step held. The other half of the
wave is that **a printed literal is a stronger attractor than the branch heading above it** — a
coverage line scoped to ONE-LAND hands shipped four two-and-three-land sevens across two guides,
and a floor's engine-marked dead forms scored nine correct declines as breaks.

168. THE LITERAL AUDIT IS THE REVIEWER'S FIRST STEP, NOT A CARRY-LIST ITEM, AND IT REPORTS THE
    COUNT OF MEETINGS WITH THE **NEW** STRING. Three deck123 sentences and one deck126 rule went
    false in a single engine wave: "the Slip's target rows print no DIES / SURVIVES" (lane L now
    prints it — `123 vs152` s10 `-1/-1 - DIES`, `123 vs146` s19 three `- SURVIVES (toughness N,
    -1/-1 more kills it)` rows), `[already owned:` (**0 renders corpus-wide**, replaced by three
    brackets), the bare `[from exile]` (now a clause), and deck126's Lantern rule, which declined
    **9 of 9** `[already owned:` rows in wave 51 and took **5 of 5** `[second copy:` rows here
    with its text unchanged (`deck123/skill.md` S1, `deck125/skill.md` S2, `deck152/skill.md` S5;
    the wave-52 carry-list asked for the re-key and got it at two guides). Rule: (a) every
    emitter string a guide quotes is written so a script can check it — exact, inside backticks,
    on its own line; (b) the reviewer's FIRST pass is a grep of every quoted literal against the
    new corpus, before any judgement is spent; (c) the pass reports THREE numbers per literal —
    old-string renders (expect 0 after a retirement), new-string renders, and takes-under-the-new-
    string — because a re-key that nobody meets is not evidence the rule fires. Companion to
    #139/#154: #154 made the re-key mandatory in the same wave; this makes it the first thing
    done and gives it a falsifiable read-out.

169. A REPLACED CLAUSE ANSWERS THE QUESTION ITS AUTHOR ASKED, NOT THE QUESTION THE OLD CLAUSE
    ANSWERED — RE-KEY BY QUESTION, NEVER BY POSITION. `[already owned: Intruder Alarm on your
    battlefield - this finds only an enchantment card]` told the pilot the card was **DEAD**
    (a value verdict). Its replacement `[second copy: you already control Intruder Alarm; both
    stay on the battlefield - no legend rule]` tells the pilot the cast is **LEGAL** (a rules
    verdict). Both are true; only the first carried the verdict the pilot's question needed, and
    a second Intruder Alarm was cast **4 times in 14 rows** (`123 vs125` s41 at 15 life, s59 at 6,
    `123 vs126` s74, `123 vs162` s39) against 1 in 68 under the old wording — Intruder Alarm's
    primitive is `lord(creature) doesnotuntap` plus two `@movedTo(creature|...):untap all(creature)`
    triggers, so a second copy adds nothing (`deck123/skill.md` S2, `deck126/skill.md` S7,
    `deck125/skill.md` S2). Rule, as a companion to the trust doctrine: never teach doubt of the
    render, AND never assume a reworded tag carries the old tag's verdict. At every re-key the
    reviewer asks *what question does the new string answer*, and where the new string answers a
    different one, the guide supplies the missing verdict itself. ⚠ The same check protects
    against the mirror error: `Chromatic Lantern`'s `[second copy:` takes are NOT dead casts —
    its primitive carries five own `{T}:Add` abilities beside the non-stacking `lord(land)`, so a
    second Lantern is a real mana source and the guide's objection to it is a deck judgment, not
    a dead-row verdict.

170. A RULE LIVES ON THE WINDOW THAT CAN STILL REFUSE. `123 vs146` s18: the CAST row
    `Cast Tragic Slip {b} {right now: -1/-1 (no creature has died this turn, so Morbid does NOT
    apply)} ... - legal targets right now: Nadaar, Selfless Paladin, Triumphant Adventurer,
    Goblin` was refusable and carried no verdict; s19's target ask printed
    `- SURVIVES (toughness N, -1/-1 more kills it)` on all three rows above the sentence **"this
    ask has no pass row"** — the card was already spent (`deck123/skill.md` S3). Corpus-wide:
    **85 `Cast Tragic Slip` rows carry no DIES/SURVIVES; 9 target rows carry it.** Rule: when the
    losing choice is made on a FORCED ask, the guide's rule belongs on the row that OPENED it and
    says so in the prompt's own words ("the target ask that follows has no pass row"); a rule
    written at the forced window cannot fire. The render half (the kill summary on the cast row)
    is the wave-53 docket's D5 — and #157's discipline applies while it is open: the guide states
    the decision rule, never doubt of the row.

171. A TEST NAMED UNDER ONE BRANCH IS APPLIED TO ITS NEIGHBOURS, AND A RUNG THAT ENDS IN A FLOOR
    MAY NOT BE FOLLOWED BY A QUALIFIER IN THE SAME RUNG. Second and third corpus of the same
    shape, now in **two guides at once**: deck146's STEP 2 and deck152's MULLIGAN section each
    put the engine's `"Playing every land in this hand would not cover any spell in it"` line
    inside their ONE-LAND ship, and both carry an explicit floor above it ("KEEP a 7 or a 6 with
    2-5 lands"; "TWO OR MORE LANDS ... KEEP. That is the floor and it is not a close call"). Four
    of the six mulligans taken at those seats were **two- and three-land** hands shipped under
    that header line — `146v123` s1 (2 lands), `146v162` s1 (2), `146v126` s2 (3, at (keeping 6),
    a bare `CHOICE: 2` with no PLAN), `152v126` s1 (2) — and deck123's `v130` s1 shipped a
    `2 lands, 5 spells` seven on the same qualifier (`deck146/skill.md` S1, `deck123/skill.md`
    S4). Rule: (a) any guide sentence quoting an engine literal states, in the same sentence,
    what the literal does NOT decide ("at two or more lands that line is not a ship"); (b) a
    qualifier goes on the rung it governs or carries its own scope — never immediately after a
    floor; (c) #131's twelve hands are constructed at every rung whose text CHANGED, not only
    for a new section. A printed literal is the most concrete thing on the screen and a branch
    heading two lines above it is not a strong enough fence.

172. A PLAN TEMPLATE THAT CARRIES A COMPUTED NUMBER GIVES EACH **INPUT** ITS OWN SLOT. `123 vs162`
    s33 filled `PLAN: stop at M = <L + C + 3>; M is <M> now; this window: <x<N> / pass>` as
    *"Stop creating humans at M=40 (L+C+3 = 20+2+3=25)"* — the slot and the template's own
    formula, present in one line, disagreeing by 15, on a row reading `[repeat: you control 23
    creatures ...]`; the take went 15 past the stop (`deck123/skill.md` S5). Rule: write
    `L <>, C <>, stop <L+C+3>` so the contradiction is visible on the line and checkable by a
    reviewer's grep. The parser half (a `plan_arithmetic_conflict` re-ask) was filed and is LOW
    on the wave-53 docket; the template change is free and belongs to the guide.

173. A RULE WHOSE TRIGGER IS A **PRICE** QUOTES THE ROW'S PRINTED NUMBER AND NEVER RESTATES THE
    FORMULA THAT PRODUCES IT. `deck125 vs162` s97 (turn 20, **3 life**): every row on the menu
    carried `[DRAW PRICE: casting this draws YOU 7 cards (their Forced Fruition), and their
    Underworld Dreams deals you 7]`; the guide's rule read "cast a counter ONLY when that price
    is below your life minus 1" — correct, and stated as arithmetic over two facts the pilot has
    to find and combine. The reply cast Essence Scatter, the seq-98 events show seven draws, and
    the seat went 3 -> 2 -> 1 -> 0 (`deck125/skill.md` S1). The positive control is s91: the same
    menu at the same life one turn earlier, all seven rows declined. Rule: *a rule that needs a
    quantity the render already prints is written as "read X off the row and compare it with Y",
    and the guide never restates the formula that produces X.* Third instance of the family
    (#155's two printed numbers, #156's printed count); the render half — the lethal tail on the
    price clause — is wave-53 D3.

174. A CARD WHOSE TEXT IS A CONDITIONAL THE PILOT COULD READ BACKWARDS GETS AN EXPLICIT FALSE
    SENTENCE IN THE GUIDE'S ALWAYS-FALSE VOICE. `deck126 vs125` s152-s216: the battlefield line
    printed Exquisite Blood's own text verbatim (`{effect: "Whenever an opponent loses life, you
    gain that much life."}`) in all 132 prompts after it resolved, and the pilot wrote — and
    carried for **nine turns** — *"their Staff of Nin ping deals 1 damage to me, triggering
    Exquisite Blood, causing me to gain 1 life, which triggers Sanguine Bond to deal 1 damage to
    them. This loop will drain them to 0."* The primitive is `@lifelostfoeof(player):life:thatmuch
    controller` — it fires when the OPPONENT loses life; being pinged fires nothing. The seat
    answered `Cast nothing right now` at 9, 5, 3, 1 and 1 life with `Cast Wall of Omens` on the
    menu (`deck126/skill.md` S4). Rule: for drain loops, "whenever you gain" / "whenever an
    opponent loses" pairs, reflexive damage and punisher enchantments, the guide names the WRONG
    direction as a sentence the pilot can fail, in the same voice as its other ALWAYS-FALSE
    lines. This extends the always-false construction from *plans* ("ramp to Emrakul") to *rules
    readings*, and the render cannot supply it — the render printed the true text and was read
    backwards anyway.

175. A WIN CONDITION IS A LIST OF **STARTERS THE PILOT OWNS**, AND THE GUIDE STATES WHAT TO DO
    WHEN THE LIST IS EMPTY. Same game. deck126's Rule #2 listed five ways to press the win and
    every one needs a card of the pilot's (a Tribute with a victim, a block, a Staff ping, a
    lifelink attack). On turns 30-38 none existed — the opponent's board held **zero creatures**
    for 17 turns (so 178 of that seat's 218 decisions were the single `Cast Tribute to Hunger
    {right now: they control 0 creatures - at 0 this does nothing}` window), the seat's own Staff
    was countered in the same events block, no Sorin, no Vampire — and the guide's only remaining
    instruction was a win-button section that reads "you have already won" (`deck126/skill.md`
    S5). Rule: every combo guide carries an explicit **no-starter branch** beside its win button:
    name the state ("assembled but unable to trigger"), name the digging action, forbid the pass.
    Without it, "you win the moment X happens" degrades into "wait for X".

176. THE PLAN LINE IS AN **INPUT** TO THE NEXT DECISION, SO THE GUIDE ASKS FOR A FORWARD INTENT,
    NEVER A CLAIM ABOUT THE CURRENT BOARD. `deck126 vs146` s11 -> s12 -> s13: the s11 reply wrote
    a 1,500-character self-arguing PLAN ending *"Both combo pieces (Exquisite Blood and Sanguine
    Bond) are now on the battlefield"* — Sanguine Bond had been exiled by Vanishing Verse at t11
    — and that exact text was re-served as `YOUR PLAN (as you last stated it)` at s12 and s13;
    the s12 decision (a redundant second Exquisite Blood at 11 life over a live Tribute row) was
    made on it (`deck126/skill.md` S6). deck126's Rule #3 already told the pilot to read both
    names off the battlefield LINE before writing "both enchantments" and it did not stop this.
    Rule: a guide's plan-shape sentence asks for what the pilot will DO next, with the board fact
    stated as the condition to re-read ("if <name> is still on your battlefield line"), never as
    an assertion the next window inherits. The reply-rules half is routed to the core prompt
    (general-strategy R146) and the staleness half to the render (wave-53 D12) — a board claim
    is exactly what goes stale between windows, and one sentence corrupted three of them.

177. THE DECIDING-SITUATIONS LIST IS A MECHANICAL DERIVATION OF THE PROSE RULES; EVERY CONDITION
    IN THE PROSE APPEARS IN ITS BULLET. `130 vs146` s35 lost the game. The COMBAT prose read
    "When that attacker is a DRAW PUNISHER named on the 'DRAW PUNISHERS' line, **or the only
    creature hitting you**, and your life minus its 'deals N' is 5 or less, put every blocker the
    clause counts on it"; the DECIDING SITUATIONS bullet — the recognise->do line the executor
    pattern-matches — dropped the second branch. The window that arrived was the second branch:
    a lone `Silverquill Silencer (3/2) deals 3 [GANG BLOCK: any 2 of yours together deal 2,
    enough to kill this attacker]`, three Goblins listed, 8 life, `you would be at 5`. Answer:
    `BLOCKS: none` (`deck130/skill.md` S6). Rule: at review time diff the two surfaces — every
    condition in a prose rule must appear in the matching bullet, or the bullet wins and the
    prose is dead text. Companion to #158 (the fix is order) and #133/#138 (the executor runs the
    list).

178. WHEN A RULE'S INPUT IS A COUNT READ OFF A BATTLEFIELD OR OPTION LINE, THE GUIDE SHOWS ONE
    COLLAPSED-HANDLE EXAMPLE AND STATES THE ARITHMETIC. deck130's central gate ("while the
    opponent's battlefield shows FOUR OR FEWER lands") was broken **8 times in 19** land-
    destruction casts. The lines it is read against print `Glacial Fortress; Island #1-#5 x5;
    Plains #1-#5 x5; Seachrome Coast [tapped]` — nine to twelve lands in four visual rows — and
    the header prints only `(19 permanents listed, of which 1 is a creature ...)` (`130 vs125`
    s61, s70, s75, s95, s97, s100; `deck130/skill.md` S7). Handles are now on cast rows, ability
    rows, attacker rows, blocker rows, sacrifice rows and battlefield lines. Rule: quote the
    collapsed form once in the sentence that gates on it and say `#1-#5 x5` counts as five. The
    render half (a land count in the header) is wave-53 D14; the guide sentence ships first and
    stays correct afterwards.

179. A PROHIBITION ON A CARD NAMES WHAT THE CARD IS BEING HELD **FOR**, IN THE SAME SENTENCE, AS
    THE ALTERNATIVE ACTION — AND A DEFENSIVE GATE CARRIES ITS OFFENSIVE HALF. Every one of
    deck130's six face-damage breaks and eight land-destruction breaks happened in a window whose
    only alternative was `Cast nothing right now` with 9-17 untapped sources (`130 vs125` s47,
    s57, s61, s70, s75, s83, s95, s97, s100). The prohibition was correct and was read; the
    sentence the model needed is that HOLDING the card IS the play. Its sibling: deck130's rule
    #0 ("never draw voluntarily against a punisher") held **59/59** windows and the deck still
    lost `v162` 0-20 to FORCED draws off two Howling Mines, with no rule naming the punisher as a
    kill target (`deck130/skill.md` S8, S10). Rule: "it is dead for the rest of the game" and
    "hold it for the creature that arrives later" are different instructions to a model looking
    for something to do with its mana — write the second; and a gate the pilot cannot satisfy by
    obeying it gets the offensive half beside it ("...and the first affordable window that kills
    <the punisher> is taken").

180. A GUIDE CARRIES ONE PARAGRAPH PER POOL ARCHETYPE THAT HAS **BEATEN IT**, OR AN EXPLICIT NOTE
    THAT THE MATCHUP HAS NOT PRODUCED A LOSS. deck123's guide has had an "AGAINST A DECK THAT
    COUNTERS (deck125)" paragraph since wave 50; deck130's had none and lost `v125` 25 to -5
    across **seventy turns with zero `attackers` records in 117 decisions**, feeding one threat
    per turn into open blue mana (`deck130/skill.md` S9). The pool's archetypes are small and
    known (counters = 125; lifegain walls + converter = 126; draw punishers = 162; land
    destruction = 130; token combo = 123). Rule: the paragraph is 4-8 lines, is keyed to printed
    facts (their untapped count, their line, their log), and is EVIDENCE-GATED — written only
    for an archetype that has actually taken a game off this deck, so the roster does not become
    a matchup encyclopedia.

181. A **ROUTING RULE** (which row to take) AND A **REPORTING RITUAL** (write this sentence) ARE
    DIFFERENT INSTRUMENTS AND ARE SCORED DIFFERENTLY; A RITUAL IS GATED ON AN OBSERVABLE IN THE
    PROMPT, NEVER ON THE ANSWER ALONE. Wave 51 gave deck146 *"when you answer 'Cast nothing right
    now', your reply names the highest entry that was on this menu ... in the shape 'nothing right
    now: entry <number> <card name> was on this menu; it did not match because <a fact printed on
    this screen>'"*. This corpus: **20 of 84** own-turn `Cast nothing` answers carried it — and
    the decision it protects did not break at all (0 misroutes in 21 windows holding a live cast
    row), with the full form appearing exactly where it had work to do (`146 vs125` s138/s140)
    (`deck146/skill.md` S2). Rule: at this tier the routing rule is followed and the ritual is
    not, so a ritual earns its tokens only where it can change an answer — gate it on something
    the prompt prints ("AND the menu holds at least one other `Cast ...` row"). Corollary: 24% is
    the ritual's natural rate on a first statement, not decay, and #138's no-fourth-restatement
    rule still forbids buying the other 76% with repetition.

182. THERE IS A SHORT LIST OF **ENGINE-LITERAL ABSOLUTES THAT BELONG IN EVERY GUIDE**, AND THEIR
    ABSENCE IS A DEFECT FOUND AT REVIEW TIME, NOT A DECK CHOICE. deck162's guide carries *"NO
    'their untapped blockers' TAG AT ALL ON A LINE MEANS NOTHING THEY CONTROL CAN BLOCK IT ... the
    answer is SEND, every time, at every life total"* and deck162 sent 2 of 2; deck146 has no such
    line and missed 1 of 39 (`146 vs125` s107); deck152 has none and missed **5 of 19**, all five
    inside a converter rule that reads as a general prohibition (`deck146/skill.md` S3). Rule: the
    standing list is the empty blocker tag, the `[repeat:` / `[Upkeep offer:` pass forms, the
    `[legendary:` non-body, `{this hits YOUR permanent}` (179 rows, **0 taken**, pool-wide), the
    `at 0 this does nothing` decline (543 rows, **0 taken**) and the `[finds only ... none left]`
    dead-Tutor row. These are statements about what the render MEANS, and the render is the same
    for all seven seats; a reviewer adding a deck's first check-list ports them in the same pass.

183. IN A TWO-BRANCH RULE WHERE ONE BRANCH IS CATASTROPHIC AND ONE IS ORDINARY, THE BRANCHES ARE
    **SYMMETRICALLY SPECIFIED** — THE MILDER BRANCH NAMES ITS OWN ENGINE LITERAL, STATES ITS
    ACTION IN THE SAME IMPERATIVE REGISTER, AND CARRIES ITS OWN COST LINE. deck152's converter
    section: BOTH names printed -> *"ATTACK: none, every combat, fliers included - 'no creature
    they control can block this attacker' is exactly why it kills you"*; ONE name printed -> *"the
    race is real: race it with your EVASION"* — one clause, no literal, no imperative. In
    `152 vs126` only Sanguine Bond was ever in play; at s24 (their life 28) and s45 (32) the seat
    held **five** A-lines all reading `[no creature they control can block this attacker]` and its
    replies quote the both-names logic (*"attack with evasion if available (currently none)"* with
    the evasion printed in front of it) (`deck152/skill.md` S4). Rule: an asymmetric pair is read
    as one rule with a caveat. Diagnostic at review time: **strip the headings and read only the
    imperatives — if one branch has three and the other none, the pair will collapse toward the
    loud one.**

184. A FLOOR OF THE FORM "IF X IS OFFERED, TAKE ONE" ENUMERATES THE **ENGINE-MARKED DEAD FORMS OF
    X** THAT IT DOES NOT REACH. deck152's #3 RULE ("on YOUR main phase, if a creature is offered,
    cast one") produced 10 apparent breaks; **9** were menus whose only creature row was `Cast
    Katilda, Dawnhart Prime {g}{w} (1/1) [legendary: you already control Katilda, Dawnhart Prime
    - legend rule: casting this sends one copy to your graveyard]`. Declining is right there; the
    model got it right nine times against its own guide, and only `152 vs130` s7 was a real break
    (`deck152/skill.md` S6). Rule: the floor names the forms the engine already marks — `[legendary:`
    second copies, rows printing `at 0 this does nothing`, rows whose only targets are the pilot's
    own, `[finds only ... none left]` — because a floor without them scores correct play as a
    break, costs review attention, and invites an edit that would make play worse. Companion to
    #118: a "violated" rule whose breaks are all correct declines has no violations at all.

185. A RULE THAT OFFERS A **MENU OF ALTERNATIVES** STATES WHAT HAPPENS WHEN NONE OF THE POSITIVE
    ALTERNATIVES IS ON THE SCREEN, IN ITS OWN SENTENCE, WITH THE DO-NOTHING OPTION PROMOTED
    RATHER THAN TRAILING. deck162's RULE 2 brake reads *"With a Howling Mine already on your
    battlefield line, a second row reading 'converters on your battlefield: 0' is the brake: take
    a wall, a punisher, a Liliana's Caress, or 'Cast nothing right now' instead"*. Both of the
    deck's only rule breaks this corpus (`162 vs130` s11, `162 vs123` s8) came from an ask with
    **exactly two rows** — the second Mine and `Cast nothing right now`. Three of the four named
    alternatives were not on the menu; the fourth is the least imperative item in the list and
    sits last. Where the list had a body in it the brake held 13/13 (`deck162/skill.md` S7).
    Rule: write the empty case explicitly — *"a two-row ask whose only spell is <the forbidden
    one> is the brake FIRING, not the brake failing: row 2 IS the answer"*. An alternatives list
    implicitly promises one of its items will be available; the window where that promise fails
    is exactly the window where the rule is worth the most, and an empty list reads as licence.

186. THE REVIEW METHOD COUNTS **NAMED CITATIONS**, NOT ONLY BREAKS. deck162's Master-of-the-Feast
    carve-out (*"With NO punisher out, cast it ONLY when the opponent's battlefield line reads 'of
    which N are creatures' with N of 1 or more"*) was hit twice at K=0 and both takes were legal
    (`v146` s17 "of which 1 is a creature"; `v123` s10 "of which 3 are creatures"), and the s10
    reply reads: *"Currently have 0 converters, so Master of the Feast is cast only for its body
    to block the opponent's threats, as per Rule 2 exception. Do not cast draw engines yet as
    K=0."* — the rule, its condition, its literal and its scope in the pilot's own words
    (`deck162/skill.md` S8). Rule: grep the replies for each rule's own words and report the
    citation count beside the break count. A cited exception is evidence the WHOLE surrounding
    rule is being read; a rule with citations and no breaks is the strongest exit signal a guide
    can produce, and it separates "no breaks because the rule works" from "no breaks because no
    window arose" (#132's UNTESTED verdict).

**Supporting instances recorded, not amended.** deck125 S3 (the "read the row, not the total"
family at its ceiling — sweeper at the header's second number 220/220 declined, land drop 98/98,
`X = 3` 11/11, Revelation from a `max affordable X` of 1 or 2 **0/18**, TARGET asks 5/5 — against
the two rules that broke, both of which ask the pilot to compare the row against a price on a
DIFFERENT line): a measured contrast supporting #155/#173, no new rule. deck126 S7
(`[second copy:` flipping 9/9 declines into 5/5 takes): the evidence for #169, not a separate
rule. deck130's `answer_replaced` record (5/5 correct at those seats, including `130 vs152` s17
turning "Cast nothing right now" into "Cast Talisman of Impulse" after 577 s): #116 holds, no
change — and see the general-strategy R136 note, because the seat's reading of the SAME mechanism
as a false positive was itself refuted on disk. deck146's 39 empty-tag A-lines with 38 sent and
deck162's 2/2: the #182 list's first entry, already an absolute in one guide. deck152's three
`{paying this taps:}` takes in Upkeep and Main 1 (`152 vs162` s11, s19, s27, incl. a Katilda
activation that tapped three Aspirants out of the combat that followed): #155's family with a
newer literal — the guide re-key is 152-I and the render companion (the row saying the same
activation is offered again after combat) is wave-53 D-LOW. The 900-second mulligan stalls
(`126 vs146` s1, `123 vs130` s3): an engine/observability item (wave-53 D10), never a guide
question — two opening-hand decisions in this corpus were the heuristic's, not the pilot's.

---

# WAVE-53 AMENDMENTS (187-208) — the TENTH fair-hand corpus

Corpus `matchups-20260902-023342`, binary master **c628dd531** (lanes M 614312289, N 3ab5c27c4,
O 0ba5ae2eb, P 1057c7c9d, Q ba33a9adb, R 1bb08b2b1, S 6a4d5e119, T 00549b391). Pilot
**qwen36-35b-a3b** on Spark :8084. 42 seat logs, 3,572 records, **3,483 decisions**, 20/21 natural
(`152v125` HUNG — engine defect, lane X; excluded from every rate). Sources: the four wave-53 seat
files, seven `deckN/skill.md`, seven `deckN/general-suggestions.md`, and the corpus, re-derived on
disk by the synthesis step for every number quoted below.

187. **#154 GAINS A DEADLINE: A DERIVATION THAT A SHIPPED LITERAL NOW ANSWERS IS CUT IN THE SAME
    WAVE THE LITERAL FIRST RENDERS, NOT THE WAVE AFTER.** deck123's RULE 4 asked the pilot to scan
    a target name list for "toughness 2 or more" while lane O's new clause printed
    `{kills 0 of the 3 legal targets at -1/-1}` on the same row. Both surfaces were on screen at
    `123v130` s64 and the pilot cast the Slip anyway, then aimed it at a `- SURVIVES` Rorix at 1
    life (`deck123/skill.md` S1). Rule: a derivation is a second, weaker copy of the literal's
    answer, and where the two disagree inside a pilot's head the derivation is what it acts on. The
    re-key obligation #154 records is due at DEPLOY of the wave whose lane changed the string —
    which is also what the wave-51 boundary pass B3 discovered by omission, at the cost of deck126's
    Lantern rule going 9/9 -> 0/5.

188. **THE #168 LITERAL AUDIT IS COUNTED FROM THE *ROWS*, AND IT IS SCOPED PER (LITERAL, CARD
    FAMILY): A STRING THAT RENDERS 1,586 TIMES CORPUS-WIDE CAN RENDER 0 TIMES ON THE ROW THE GUIDE
    KEYED TO IT.** Two seats found the same hole from opposite ends. (a) A naive `prompt`
    scan mints phantom renders, because the `prompt` field carries the instruction block, the whole
    narration log and the pilot's own echoed PLAN as well as the option rows — the engine seat's two
    apparent "bare `ability:` stack lines" were the model's own prose quoted back inside a PLAN
    block, and deck123 counted a "render" of `a second copy changes nothing`, a string with **1 row
    render in the whole corpus** (`deck123/skill.md` S4). **Scope correction this step owes that
    seat:** its stated reason — "the guide is INSIDE the prompt" — is NOT true of this translog
    schema; the guide lives in the system message and appears in **0 of 826** `prompt` fields at its
    own seat, checked on disk. The RULE is right; its justification is the log and the plan echo,
    not the guide. (b)
    deck146's cast-order entry 5 gated Silverquill Command on *"the Command row's own `{right now:`
    text names a card it would return"*; `{right now:` renders **1,586** times corpus-wide and **0
    of 28** times on a `Cast Silverquill Command` row, so the condition was unsatisfiable, the entry
    collapsed to a lower one, and ~20 windows of a free body-plus-a-card were declined across turns
    29-83 of an 84-turn loss (`deck146/skill.md` S-1). Rule: the three-number audit reads
    `options_text` for renders and `chosen_text` for takes, says which field it read, and reports
    the numbers **per (literal, card)** pair for the family the guide's sentence is about. A literal
    alive elsewhere is not evidence the sentence can fire. Companion to #154: the re-key obligation
    applies not only when a lane CHANGES a string, but when a guide sentence was written from a
    string the emitter never attached to that card at all.

189. **A GUIDE SENTENCE KEYED TO A LITERAL THAT *COUNTS* SOMETHING NAMES WHAT IS OUTSIDE THE
    COUNT.** #171 makes a mulligan-literal sentence say what the literal does NOT decide; this
    corpus carried the same failure into pricing literals and it cost a won game.
    `130v162` s62, opponent at **1 life**, ten untapped sources: row 1 read
    `Cast Hammer of Bogardan {1}{r}{r} … {kills 0 of the 2 legal targets at 3 damage}` while the
    target ask three seconds later opened `1. The opponent (player, life 1)` — the summary counts
    creature targets only, by the emitter's own design note, and 3 to the face was the game
    (`deck123/skill.md` S2, `deck130/skill.md` grounding). Rule: "kills 0" means "kills 0
    CREATURES"; "N permanents listed, of which K are creatures" is not a hand count; "max affordable
    X" is not the X you can afford AFTER this cast. One clause, on the rung that reads the literal.
    The render half is a docket item (D3 below); the guide sentence must stay correct either way.

190. **#177'S PROSE-VS-BULLET DIFF RUNS AS PART OF EACH EDIT, NOT AS A PASS AT THE END, AND IT
    GAINS A STEP 0: ENUMERATE THE ASK KINDS.** Two seats, two halves. (a) The reviewer who WRITES an
    exception is the only person who knows every place it lands: deck125's Path carve-out
    contradicted two DECIDING-SITUATIONS bullets the moment it was written and its Fruition
    threshold contradicted a bullet three sections earlier, and four of that seat's 27 edits exist
    only because the diff was run late (`deck125/skill.md` S3). (b) The diff as written only catches
    a bullet that DROPPED a branch; it does not catch a rule the recognise->do list never mentions
    at all. deck146's cleanup-discard order is a correct, complete twelve-line bullet filed inside
    the MULLIGAN section, five hundred lines above the ask it governs, with no cleanup bullet in
    DECIDING SITUATIONS; `146v130` discarded at three consecutive cleanups with **Emeria's Call on
    all three numbered lists** and never sent it (**0 of 3**), and the seat died at 0 against an
    opponent on 2 (`deck146/skill.md` S-3). Rule: step 0 of the diff enumerates every ASK KIND the
    seat's corpus produced (`ask`, `priority`, `attackers`, `blockers`, `discard`, `reveal`,
    `bottom`) and checks that each one the guide has a rule for is named in the recognise->do list
    **by the literal the prompt prints for that ask** (here `"your hand has N cards and your maximum
    hand size is 7"`). A rule filed under the wrong heading is dead text in exactly the way #177
    describes.

191. **A CARVE-OUT IS CONSTRUCTED AND CHECKED FOR REACHABILITY: THE EXCEPTION'S ALLOWED ACTIONS AND
    THE PRIMARY RULE'S REQUIREMENT GO IN THE SAME SENTENCE.** #131 constructs the twelve hands at
    every rung whose text changed; exceptions need the same treatment. deck123's RULE 2 said "a
    colour at 0 comes first" and then carved out "a basic, against deck130" — and Marsh Flats
    fetches only Plains or Swamp (`mtg.txt:71436` `target(*[swamp;plains]|myLibrary)`), so in the
    exact case where the carve-out fired (`123v130` s36, `{u}` at 0, two `{2}{u}` Intruder Alarms in
    hand, Tundra and Underground Sea both on the menu and both making {U}) **no action inside the
    carve-out could satisfy the rule above it**. The pilot took the carve-out and lost the game
    (`deck123/skill.md` S3). Rule: for each exception, one line — the exception's allowed actions
    and the primary rule's requirement, stated together. Where they cannot both be satisfied, the
    exception needs its own escape ("…unless a dual on the list is your only source of that
    colour"), or it is a trap the guide built.

192. **A THRESHOLD IS A CONSTANT COMPARED AGAINST A NUMBER THE RENDER ALREADY PRINTS — NEVER A
    RELATION BETWEEN TWO MOVING TOTALS THE PILOT MUST COMBINE.** deck125's only loss is a rule that
    was *followed* and was *wrong*: under Forced Fruition the guide said "cast a counter ONLY when
    that price is below your life minus 1"; at 24 life the printed price was 14, the relation held,
    and the seat paid 58% of its life to deny 1 damage per future card (`125v162` seq 78, seat at
    10 by seq 79, dead at t21 without casting again) (`deck125/skill.md` S1). Rule: a relation
    between two moving numbers is satisfied over a huge, mostly-wrong region the pilot cannot see —
    it can only evaluate the relation at one point. A constant read against a printed finished
    number (`- you would be at K`; take it only when K >= 15) is checkable, is falsifiable in the
    next corpus, and cannot silently widen. Corollary for reviewers: **when a rule is followed and
    the game is still lost, suspect the threshold's SHAPE before suspecting the pilot's reading.**

193. **WHERE THE PROMPT CARRIES BOTH A COMPOSITE SURFACE AND A DEDICATED ONE FOR THE SAME FACT, KEY
    THE GUIDE TO THE DEDICATED LINE AND SAY SO EXPLICITLY.** Three of deck125's rules pointed at
    substrings inside a composite line — *"read the OPPONENT battlefield line for an [enchantment]
    whose {effect:} reads 'Whenever an opponent loses life…'"* — while the prompt separately printed
    `LIFE-TO-DAMAGE CONVERTER on the battlefield: theirs - Sanguine Bond`, a dedicated single-purpose
    line, **353 times in the game where the rule then broke twice** at a cost of 30 life
    (`125v126` seq 294 and 332, after four correct declines of the identical row on the identical
    board) (`deck125/skill.md` S2). Rule: the composite key fails by CROWDING — a 25-permanent
    battlefield listing buries the substring — while a dedicated line is one string at a fixed
    place. Key to it, and write the negative ("you do not read the battlefield for it") so the old
    reading cannot come back.

194. **A GUIDE REFUSES "NOTHING ELSE ON THE MENU WAS CASTABLE" BY NAME, ONCE, AND CITES THE SEAT'S
    OWN BIGGEST DECLINE CEILING AS PROOF A DECLINE IS A NORMAL ANSWER.** Both of deck125's low-X
    Revelation casts (`125v126` seq 59, `125v123` seq 17) and both of deck126's zero-Tribute casts
    (`126v125` seq 73/74) happened on menus where **every other cast row was one the guide forbids**
    — the pilot treats a menu with one legal-looking row as an instruction to take it
    (`deck125/skill.md` S4). Rule: state, once, that a menu on which nothing is worth casting is
    answered with the decline row, and prove it with the seat's own number (deck125: **155 sweeper
    windows at a header second number of 0, 0 taken**; corpus-wide `at 0 this does nothing` **613
    rows, 2 taken**). This is #185's empty-alternatives sentence generalised from one rule to the
    menu itself.

195. **WHEREVER A GUIDE LISTS THE MEMBERS OF A MECHANICAL CLASS, NAME AT LEAST ONE PLAUSIBLE
    NON-MEMBER AND SAY WHAT IT DOES INSTEAD.** deck126's Rule #2 listed five ways to press the win
    button; at `126v146` seq 21 the pilot invented a sixth, writing that an Overgrown Battlement's
    block would gain 2 life and start the loop. The rule was not missing a branch — it was missing
    the sentence that says the other walls gain nothing (`mtg.txt:83596`: Overgrown Battlement has
    no life clause; only Perimeter Captain `mtg.txt:85398` and Pride Guardian `mtg.txt:88356` do)
    (`deck126/skill.md` S6). Rule: at this tier **a list of what works reads as an incomplete list
    of what works.** The negative is what stops the pilot generalising the class outward under
    pressure; it is the "the thought X is ALWAYS FALSE" device of #174 applied to card lists rather
    than to plans.

196. **WHEN A DECISION'S PROSE IS RIGHT AND ITS CODED ANSWER IS WRONG, THE GUIDE EDIT BELONGS IN THE
    ANSWER-FORMAT SECTION AND THE DETECTOR BELONGS IN THE ENGINE LIST.** `126v125` seq 73 and 74,
    two consecutive replies on a two-row menu whose row 1 read
    `Cast Tribute to Hunger {2}{b} {right now: they control 0 creatures - at 0 this does nothing}`:
    both wrote `CHOICE: 1 (Cast Tribute to Hunger)` and both wrote a PLAN line arguing against
    exactly that ("The opponent has no creatures, so Tribute to Hunger does nothing. Pass the
    turn."). Both executed; no `answer_replaced`, no parse note (`deck126/skill.md` S7). Rule: the
    card rule was known, stated, and being recited at the moment it was broken, so **no card-level
    sentence could have helped.** What the guide can carry is a format check — read the number you
    wrote against the sentence you are about to write after it — and the counterpart is an ADDITIVE
    engine stamp (a PLAN line that contradicts the chosen row's own annotation), never a suppression.

197. **A RENDER RE-KEY CAN CLOSE A RULE THE GUIDE COULD NOT: MAKE THE TAG ANSWER THE QUESTION THE
    PILOT IS ASKING, AND THE GUIDE SENTENCE THEN ONLY HAS TO POINT AT IT.** Wave 52 recorded a rule
    that went from 9-of-9 declines to 0-of-5 when its recognition string was retired underneath it.
    This corpus, lane P printed a *partial-redundancy* tag stating the consequence —
    `…, but the effect it gives your OTHER permanents is already on - this copy adds only its own
    abilities` — and deck126 declined **6 of 6**, including three windows where the second Chromatic
    Lantern was the ONLY cast row on the menu, at 18, 10 and 1 life, **with no guide change at all**
    (`deck126/skill.md` S8). Rule: when a tag answers a rules question the pilot did not ask
    (legality), the cheapest fix is to make it answer the question the pilot IS asking ("does this
    copy DO anything?"). This inverts the usual direction — sometimes the cheapest guide edit is a
    render change plus a two-word pointer — and it is why #168's re-key obligation is worth its cost.

198. **A BREAK RATE IS REPORTED WITH THE NUMBER OF DISTINCT TURNS THE BREAKS OCCUPY.** deck126's
    zero-stop broke "2 of 39", which reads like a 5% slip; both breaks are in the **same turn of the
    same game, two windows apart, at the same life total, off byte-identical menus** — one failure
    with two records, and an edit sized for a 5% slip is the wrong size (`deck126/skill.md` S9).
    Rule: a seat file that reports `N of M` also reports the distinct (game, turn) count. Companion
    to #87/#167's counts-not-rates discipline and to #101's clustering note: consecutive records
    inside one turn are one decision observed repeatedly, not independent trials.

199. **IN ANY GUIDE RULE THAT IS A TOP-DOWN PROCEDURE, THE STEP THAT WINS THE GAME IS STEP 0 AND
    OVERRIDES THE REST OF THE RULE — INCLUDING ITS OWN LATCHES AND FLOORS.** deck130's #2 RULE ran
    "1. planeswalker -> 2. a creature it kills -> 3. a creature that is hurting you -> 4. the face,
    only at 6 or less", under a heading reading "DAMAGE GOES AT THEIR CREATURES AND PLANESWALKERS,
    NOT THE FACE". Every step was correct and the ordering lost a won game: at `Opponent life: 1`
    the pilot walked the list from the top and put a 3-damage Hammer into a 3-loyalty planeswalker
    (`130v162` s62 -> s63), then declined a lethal Pyrite Spellbomb at s65 (`{R}{S}: Damage:2
    target(anytarget)`, `mtg.txt:90168`), and died at 0 to 1 nine windows later
    (`deck130/skill.md` S6). Rule: **a discipline rule that can outrank "you win now" is mis-ordered,
    however well each step is written.** Review corollary: for every ordered procedure in a guide,
    construct the state where the LAST step is lethal and check that the earlier steps do not consume
    the resource.

200. **#132 HAS A THIRD VERDICT — UNTESTABLE-AT-THIS-SEAT — AND IT EARNS THE SECTION A
    COMPRESSION, NOT A DELETION AND NOT A RESTATEMENT.** The wave-52 boundary pass set an explicit
    condition on deck130's mulligan section: if a third corpus produced no 2+-land `would not cover`
    look, the check moves off the guide. It did — **6 looks, 6 keeps, 0 ships, 0 bottom asks, 0
    renders of the branch, three corpora** (`deck130/skill.md` S7). Rule: "the check moves off the
    guide" means (a) the section is no longer scored per corpus, (b) the RULE stays, because the
    branch is still reachable and the render can still produce it, and (c) its supporting ANECDOTE
    may be compressed — a story about a hand that never comes is the cheapest text in a 27-38 KB
    file to lose. Making (c) explicit is what stops each wave's reviewer from either re-litigating
    the rule or growing it.

201. **A FRACTION WHOSE DENOMINATOR INCLUDES ENGINE-MARKED-DEAD ROWS IS NOT THE RULE'S FRACTION:
    REPORT BOTH NUMBERS AND SCORE THE LIVE ONE.** deck146's show-the-work ritual scored **15 of
    165** own-turn `Cast nothing` answers that held another `Cast …` row — a 9% rate that reads like
    decay. Split: **139** of the 165 held only rows the engine itself had annotated dead
    (`at 0 this does nothing` 613 renders / 2 takes corpus-wide; `[legendary:` 12 / 0), which the
    guide's own text already excuses; the live remainder is **26**, of which 20 are one real lane
    and six are guide-legal declines. The ritual therefore had **0** decisions to protect and the
    honest verdict was DELETE (`deck146/skill.md` S-2). Rule: extends #109 and #184 — report
    `15/165 raw, 15/26 live` and score the second. #181's ritual gate is applied with the
    denominator corrected, or a correct rule is scrapped for a number that was never its own.

202. **AN ABSOLUTE KEYED TO A SUBSTRING THAT THE EMITTER PRINTS ONCE PER *LIST MEMBER* CARRIES THE
    LIST'S CARDINALITY, OR IT FIRES ON EVERY MEMBER AT ONCE.** deck152's converter rule read *"hold
    every creature whose tag prints one `(blocking trigger:`"*. An A-line's tag is an ENUMERATION:
    `their untapped blockers: Wall of Omens (0/4) (you kill it, your attacker lives); Vampire (1/1)
    (you kill it, your attacker lives (lifelink: they gain 1, and their converter takes 1 off you))`.
    One gain clause anywhere in that list held the whole attacker, including a 4/4 and a 7/5 whose
    first listed blocker traded itself away for free. `152v126` s26 (31 life vs 17), s32 (25 vs 16),
    s40 (17 vs 16): four A-lines, **two** distinct blocker names, two attackers declared, every
    time; their life moved 17 -> 16 -> 16 and the seat lost 0-21 (`deck152/skill.md` S-1). Rule: the
    sentence states what the list's LENGTH means as well as what its members say — "count the
    distinct names in `their untapped blockers`; that is how many of your attackers they can block
    at all." Companion to #178 and #183: the correction to an over-aggressive absolute is a PRICE
    COMPARISON, not a mirrored prohibition, or the next corpus breaks the other way — which is
    exactly what happened after wave 52 closed the `ATTACK: none` half of this same rule.

203. **#171'S SCOPING SENTENCE JOINS THE #182 STANDING PORT LIST, AND #144'S CROSS-GUIDE GREP IS RUN
    AS A MATCHED PAIR: WHEN ONE GUIDE HOLDS A SHARED LITERAL AT ZERO BREAKS AND ANOTHER BREAKS ON
    IT, THE PASSING GUIDE'S SENTENCE IS THE FIX AND THE PORT IS A COPY.** Same corpus, same literal,
    two guides, opposite results. deck146's STEP 2 carries *"THAT COVERAGE LINE IS A ONE-LAND TEST
    AND NOTHING ELSE. Read the engine's land count FIRST. At TWO OR MORE lands the sentence … is not
    a ship and never was"* and shipped **0** two-or-three-land sevens. deck152 carries a STRONGER
    floor (*"TWO OR MORE LANDS AND AT LEAST ONE SPELL: KEEP. That is the floor and it is not a close
    call"*) plus an explicit FORBIDDEN THOUGHT naming the colour argument, quotes the coverage
    literal only under its ONE LAND rung — and shipped `152v162` s1 (2 lands making {G}{G}, five
    white spells) with the reply *"Mulligan for a hand with at least one white mana source"*, the
    forbidden thought verbatim. Third corpus of that exact shape (`deck152/skill.md` S-2). Rule:
    a stronger floor is not a substitute for a scoping sentence on the literal that argues against
    it. Second half, new here: **the coverage line collapses two different causes into one string** —
    too few lands, and enough lands of the wrong colour — and the second is the case a two-colour
    deck meets most often, so the scoping sentence names the COLOUR cause explicitly or the pilot
    reads the literal as agreement with the thought the guide forbids. (The render half — say which
    cause — is a docket item; the guide sentence is due either way.)

204. **#157'S SHARED-FACT RE-DERIVATION RUNS ON A RULE'S *SURVIVING* BREAKS EVEN WHEN THE BREAK
    COUNT IS FALLING, AND THE MISSING CONDITION MAY BE A CARDINALITY INSIDE THE LITERAL THE RULE
    ALREADY QUOTES.** deck152's `{paying this taps:` stop went 3 takes (wave 52) -> 2 takes
    (wave 53) out of 12 windows. Both survivors share a printed fact the rule does not name: **the
    clause holds exactly ONE name and the row puts a strictly bigger body on the board**
    (`152v130` s11 Ranger Class -> a 2/2 Wolf, s14 Sigarda 4/4, each tapping one 1/1 Katilda; that
    game was won 11 to -4). Every row the seat correctly passed either named two or three creatures
    or attached its one name to a level counter, an activation or a removal spell
    (`deck152/skill.md` S-3). Rule: run #157's shared-fact step BEFORE any restatement, and accept a
    CARDINALITY read off the literal the rule already quotes as the missing condition — it costs the
    guide a clause, not a paragraph. Companion to #184: **a floor whose surviving "breaks" are all
    correct play is over-broad, not under-stated.**

205. **A SURVIVAL GATE LIVES AT THE ASK KIND THAT *SPENDS* THE RESOURCE, NOT AT THE ASK KIND WHERE
    THE LOSS BECOMES VISIBLE.** deck162's survival arithmetic is correct and complete — *"SURVIVAL
    COMES FIRST, AND IT IS ARITHMETIC - RUN IT BEFORE THE NUMBERED RULES BELOW"*, four numbered
    steps — and it sits under `RULE 4 - BLOCKING`. At `162v152` s11 (turn 10, **4 life**, five
    untapped sources, own header `of which 0 are creatures`, their header `4 of them without a
    restriction against attacking`) the seat was offered Ob Nixilis `{leaves 0 of your 5}`, Master of
    the Feast `{leaves 2 of your 5}` and Shield Sphere `{leaves 5 of your 5}` on ONE menu; Master
    and Sphere were affordable together, i.e. two blockers. It took Ob Nixilis, tapped out, and at
    s14 the block window ran the survival arithmetic perfectly and concluded *"There is no way to
    survive this combat"* (`deck162/skill.md` S-1). Rule: for every gate phrased as survival, ask
    which ASK KIND spends the resource the gate needs and put the gate there — **the block window
    inherits a board the cast window bought.** Concretely: write it against the numbers printed on
    the CAST prompt and make it numbered step 0 of the cast order (#165), not a paragraph under a
    different heading (#158).

206. **#183'S IMPERATIVE-COUNT DIAGNOSTIC IS RUN ON THE *EDIT*, NOT ONLY ON THE GUIDE: CLOSING A
    RULE'S EMPTY CASE CREATES A MIRROR FAILURE ON ITS EXEMPT CASE UNLESS BOTH BRANCHES GET
    IMPERATIVES IN THE SAME EDIT.** Wave 52 shipped #185 at deck162 — *"a two-row ask whose only
    spell is a second engine at K of 0 is the brake FIRING, not the brake failing: row 2 IS the
    answer"* — three imperatives, a WHAT-THIS-COST, its own paragraph. The rule's EXEMPTION (the
    FIRST Howling Mine is cast at K of 0) stayed a half-sentence with none. Result this corpus:
    second Mines declined **3/3** at K=0 and taken **4/4** at K>=1, the brake working perfectly,
    while the untagged FIRST Mine was declined on a two-row menu **11 times across three games**,
    arriving four turns late twice — against a wave-52 over-brake count of **1**
    (`deck162/skill.md` S-2). Rule: after writing a fix for one branch, strip the headings and count
    the imperatives on each branch of the pair; where the branches are "the rule fires" and "the
    rule is exempt", both need the same register and **both need the printed discriminator named**
    (here it is exact and free: a second copy's row carries `[second copy: …]` and a first copy's
    does not).

207. **TRUST-DOCTRINE BOUNDARY: THE CARRIED `YOUR PLAN` BLOCK IS NOT A RENDER, AND A GUIDE MAY TELL
    THE PILOT TO PREFER A `{right now: …}` CLAUSE OVER ITS OWN CARRIED PLAN.** "Never teach doubt of
    the render" governs what the ENGINE states about the game. The `YOUR PLAN` block is the pilot's
    own older text quoted back verbatim, and since lane N it arrives with the engine's own age stamp
    (`as you last stated it, N windows ago on turn T`; **3,329 renders, 0 unstamped**) — the engine's
    explicit statement that the text is OLD and unchecked. `kReplyProtocol` now says the same thing
    in the model's own instructions. A guide sentence preferring the current clause over the carried
    plan therefore breaches nothing (`deck123/skill.md` S5). **Stated with the correction the records
    force:** the repro deck123 offered for this (`123v130` s57 -> s63/s64, "a 2,000-character plan
    replayed as current") does NOT hold — the served plan at s63 and s64 is **151 characters** and
    contains no Morbid claim; `consumePlan` anchors on the LAST `PLAN:` marker and bounds the block
    at 1,600 characters, and both worked. The real instance of the class is `162v152` s11 -> s12
    (a plan naming a card the row it took had just made unaffordable) and `125v126` seq 294/332
    (recognition drift across repeats of an identical board). The carve-out is adopted on those.

208. **A SEAT FILE'S "N of M" IS RE-DERIVED FROM THE FIELD THE CLAIM IS ABOUT BEFORE IT ENTERS A
    LEDGER, BECAUSE THREE HONEST DENOMINATORS PRODUCE THREE DIFFERENT TRUE NUMBERS.** This corpus
    produced four instances in one wave. `[DRAW PRICE:` lethal tails: **85 row-instances / 71
    records / 15 rows carrying `this KILLS you` / 8 RECORDS carrying it** — one seat reported
    "0 of 58" (true: its own two decks run only the cost-phrasing form, which the emitter never
    tails), one reported "8/8" (true: records at its seat), one reported "16" (not reproducible on
    either denominator). Menus that collapse to <= 2 shapes: **3** masking only `#N`, **5** masking
    every digit, **16** counting de-duplicated lists of length 1 at any row count. Opponent-turn
    zero-cast phases: **six phases / 365 windows / 3,269 s** or **seven / 445 / 3,939** depending on
    whether Blockers and Combat-damage are counted. Identical-declined runs: 26.0% / 26.2% / 27.6%
    across three grouping rules. Rule: a seat file states the FIELD (`options_text` vs `prompt` vs
    `chosen_text`), the UNIT (row-instance vs record vs window) and the MASK it counted with;
    synthesis re-derives every load-bearing number and names who was right on which denominator.
    None of the four disagreements above was an error — each was a different question — and each
    would have become a wrong docket line if quoted forward unexamined.

**Supporting instances recorded, not amended.** deck146's 595-second mulligan (`146v125` s1, the
corpus's longest single decision): the reply is 1,600 characters of self-argument that reverses once
and reaches the CORRECT answer, and the parser honoured its last coded line — **#116 holds**, and
the cost is an observability item (ledger D8), never a guide question. deck162's #186 citation count
worked a second time (RULE 2's Master-of-the-Feast carve-out met at K=1 and K=2, correctly declined
at K=0 against `of which 0 are creatures`, **0 breaks over 9 casts at K>=1**): evidence that #186
separates "no breaks because the rule works" from "no breaks because no window arose", no new rule.
deck146's P1 clean pass (**0 of N** mulligans at two or more lands, against 3 of 4 last corpus) is
the cross-guide CONTROL that makes #203 a port rather than an invention. deck123's `x22`/`x23`
repeat-row chains (4 takes, `L=…, C=…, stop=…` written 4/4, both games won) and deck130's X-menu
marker row (**taken 2/2**, second corpus): #172 and #178 at their ceilings. deck125's 155 sweeper
windows at a header second number of 0 with **0 takes**, fourth corpus, and deck130's 34 draw-punisher
windows with **0 draws taken**, third corpus: the "read the row, not the total" family holding — the
evidence under #194, not a separate rule.

---

# WAVE-54 AMENDMENTS (209-232) — the ELEVENTH fair-hand corpus

Corpus `matchups-20260903-034355`, binary master **caf023dbc** (engine lanes A e21f81de5,
B 351ad0098, C a2bc290d0, D 6c1555bb1, E 5fe998414, F 3329c40f1; wave-53 lane AA 37b7951d3 in its
first corpus; audit lanes G-N; owner O1/O2 1afe6c8f6). Pilot **qwen36-35b-a3b** on Spark :8084.
42 seat logs, **2,306 records = 42 `gamestart` + 42 `gameend` + 10 `recovery` + 2,212 decisions**
(ask 1,683 / priority 332 / attackers 99 / blockers 36 / discard 34 / reveal 20 / bottom 8).
**21/21 natural — invariant 00 satisfied for the first time since wave 52.** 23 fallbacks (1.04%),
2 Baka-executed (0.09%). Sources: the four wave-54 seat files, seven `deckN/skill.md`, seven
`deckN/general-suggestions.md`, seven `deckN/edit-texts.md`, the fifteen lane reports, and the
corpus itself — every load-bearing number below was re-derived on disk by this step with python
over the JSONL and `/usr/bin/grep` over the `.stderr` files.

**The wave's governing fact, and it is why four of these amendments are about denominators.** The
corpus's window economy is CONTAMINATED. Wave-53 lane AA's interrupt-window stall floor is
denominated in `dt` and the corpus recipe pins `WAGIC_FASTCLOCK=0.1`, so its 1,200-*game*-second
budget for an interactive-AI seat is 12,000 ticks of a headless pump: **936 of 936
`interrupt window held … for N ticks` lines read N = 12002, one value, no variance**, 468 releases,
488 `dropping stale async answer`. Every per-window rate in this corpus is measured against a
denominator that instrument moved, and the amendments below say so where it matters rather than
scoring the rates as if it had not.

209. **A GUIDE QUOTES AN ENGINE LITERAL AS A LITERAL — ON ITS OWN, NEVER DISSOLVED INTO THE
    SENTENCE'S GRAMMAR — BECAUSE THE AUDIT THAT KEEPS IT TRUE IS A GREP.** The author-side half of
    #188, and this wave paid for it twice. Lane A reworded the HOLD row; the old string
    `Hold priority - do not ask me again this turn unless the board changes` rendered **0 times in
    the whole corpus** and the new one **426 times**, and *two* guides (deck123 A54-0, deck130
    D54-0) were describing a row that no longer existed on every window they described. Both were
    caught only because the wave-54 brief mandated the B1 REVERSE audit — a guide sentence that
    paraphrases a literal into its own prose cannot be found by the audit that would have caught
    it. Rule: the quoted string is verbatim, in quotes, and nothing outside the quotes restates
    what is inside them; a sentence that needs the literal's *meaning* rather than its *bytes*
    says so and is marked family-agnostic (#210). Cost of the alternative, measured: the pool now
    carries seven guides of 40-71 KB, and a false quotation survives a whole corpus in silence.
    (deck123 S1, deck130 S5's second half; the mechanism is the same one wave-51's B3 found by
    omission.)

210. **A LITERAL THAT GAINS A CAUSE CLAUSE IS A *NEW* LITERAL EVEN THOUGH THE OLD ONE IS ITS
    PREFIX, AND THE AUDIT'S OLD-STRING COLUMN IS SCORED ON THE FULL RENDERED STRING.** Wave 53
    rendered `Playing every land in this hand would not cover any spell in it.` (10 renders). Wave
    54 rendered that sentence **0 times as a standalone** and **11 times with an appended
    parenthetical**, in two families that call for OPPOSITE decisions: `(1 land is not enough for
    your cheapest spell at mana value 2)` — a genuine count failure, ship — and `(you have 3 lands;
    no spell in it is castable off {W}{U} alone)` — a turn-one colour statement about a keepable
    hand. A guide sentence keyed to the substring still MATCHES, so a naive audit scores it live
    while it has silently become underspecified. Three guides quote that line; `152v146` s1 shipped
    a THREE-land seven under it, the fourth corpus in a row that floor has broken and the first in
    which the trigger literal itself moved. Rule: #188's audit gains a fourth column — **the
    families the new string splits into** — and any literal that gained a cause clause is either
    re-keyed to a family or explicitly marked family-agnostic in the same wave. Applies to every
    lane that adds a cause clause (this wave: C and E). (deck146 S1, deck152 152-B, seat-146 E-4.)

211. **A GUIDE'S PRESCRIBED REPLY TEMPLATE IS PART OF THE PARSER'S INPUT SURFACE, AND IT IS
    CHECKED AGAINST THE PARSER'S REVERSAL AND LATCH TESTS BEFORE IT SHIPS.** deck123's guide
    mandates a PLAN of the shape `stop <L+C+3>; M is <M> now; this window: …`. The pilot writes
    "(stop reached)" as arithmetic commentary beside a CHOICE that takes a row; the
    `decision_reversed_in_prose` / `plan_choice_conflict` detector reads a pass verdict beside a
    non-zero index and re-asks. **7 of that seat's 16 fallbacks are this collision**, four of the
    seven re-asks returned the byte-identical reply and were executed anyway
    (`plan_choice_conflict_exhausted` at `123v126` s30, s59 and `123v146` s24, s27) at a full extra
    model call each; exactly one (`123v126` s90 -> s91) was a true positive and corrected the play.
    Rule: where a guide prescribes a reply template, the action is named in exactly ONE field, and
    vocabulary that also names a ROW ("pass", "hold", "stop", "none", "nothing") may not appear
    anywhere else in the template. **This is a composition-seam defect in the promptcraft sense —
    the guide was right, the parser was right, and the pair was wrong** — which is why it belongs
    to the author of the pair and not to either half. (deck123 S2; the wave-53 analogue was the
    HOLD row's own verb colliding with the pass verdict, and that one cost 5 fallbacks.)

212. **A RUNG'S EXIT TEST IS TWO-SIDED: IT IS EXHAUSTED WHEN THE MANDATED ARTEFACT IS NEVER
    PRODUCED, *OR* WHEN IT IS PRODUCED AND THE DECISION DOES NOT CHANGE.** Wave 53 predicted that
    deck123's `Damnation: N, K, M` line, unwritten for three corpora, would retire the rung if it
    stayed at zero. It did not stay at zero: `123v125` s176 is the first reply in four corpora to
    write it — `PLAN: Damnation: N 0, K 0, M 0; cast.` — **and the dead Damnation was cast on that
    same line**, off a row already printing `{right now: destroys 0 of their creatures … 0 of
    yours}`. Compliance rose and the play did not change. Without the second clause a rung can
    absorb prose forever by improving its own compliance rate, which is the failure this seat was
    one wave away from. In BOTH cases the next edit is a render or prompt ask and the guide's
    remaining job is to shrink to the rule plus one citation. (deck123 S3; the render half is this
    wave's R-item on the all-dead menu.)

213. **WHERE A GUIDE RULE AND AN EMITTED CLAUSE CAN DISAGREE ON THE SAME BOARD, THE RULE SAYS
    WHICH WINS AND WHY — AND BEFORE A REVIEWER WRITES "THE RENDER IS FALSE" IT CHECKS THE PRIMITIVE
    *AND THE TIMING OF THE TRIGGER*, NOT ONLY THE NUMBERS.** `123v126` s88: 58 attackers, 6
    untapped blockers, opponent at 28 life. The guide's Branch B arithmetic (A >= 3B + 3) and its
    lethal override both said ATTACK. The render said `(their life LOOP is in play: any life they
    gain or you lose in this combat chains without limit - fatal to you, not a trade)`. The pilot
    obeyed the render and was RIGHT: Sanguine Bond (`mtg.txt:99004`) plus Exquisite Blood
    (`mtg.txt:37966`) is a closed loop, Pride Guardian gains 3 *on block* (`88356`) and Perimeter
    Captain 2 (`85398`), and blocking triggers resolve before combat damage, so one point of their
    gain ends the game at any attack width. The seat nearly filed this as the corpus's second
    render falsehood; two of its four candidate HIGH render items dissolved on the same check. The
    author-side obligation is the trust doctrine's, stated forward: a rule that can be contradicted
    by a clause the engine prints names the clause and yields to it in the rule text.
    (deck123 S4. Companion, and the reason this is stated twice: the reviewer-side half prevented
    a wrong docket line, and the author-side half is what stops the pilot having to arbitrate.)

214. **A CONSTANT FLOOR IS A COMPARISON WITH ONE SIDE MISSING; WHEN THE OTHER SIDE IS NOT FIXED,
    THE FIX IS A *SECOND PRINTED LITERAL THAT SORTS THE CASES*, NOT A DIFFERENT CONSTANT.** #192
    replaced deck125's moving-relation threshold with a constant read off a printed number and
    recorded that a constant cannot silently WIDEN. This corpus is the other half: it cannot
    silently NARROW either. The seat broke its new floor three times — `125v162` seq 29, 48 and 49
    at `- you would be at` K = 14, 6 and 4 — and **all three were correct plays**: seq 48 countered
    a Howling Mine and seq 49 a Teferi's Puzzle Box, permanents whose own `{target text:}` gives
    every player an extra draw every draw step under two `Whenever an opponent draws` punishers, so
    two life bought back 2 and 6+ damage *per turn for the rest of the game*. Rule: when the
    quantity on the far side of the comparison is itself variable, the guide reads a second string
    the row already prints and branches on it — here the target's own `{target text:}` for "draws
    an additional card" / "draws that many cards" — and both branches stay literal, neither becomes
    arithmetic. Companion to #192 and to #202's "the correction to an over-aggressive absolute is a
    PRICE COMPARISON, not a mirrored prohibition." (deck125 S1.)

215. **EACH STEP OF AN ORDERED PROCEDURE NAMES THE STRING ON SCREEN THAT SATISFIES IT, BECAUSE THE
    STEP THAT IS HARDEST TO EVALUATE FALLS TO THE BOTTOM OF THE LIST IN PRACTICE NO MATTER WHERE
    YOU WROTE IT.** deck125's cleanup-discard rule is a correct seven-step ordered list whose step 2
    read "a land beyond the second in hand" — a count of a zone, minus a constant. It was skipped
    in **three of the four windows where a land was on the numbered list** (`125v162` s47 at 8 life
    on a NINE-land battlefield; `125v126` s73 at t23 on TEN lands, the turn before an uncountered
    Sanguine Bond; `125v126` s80 on TWELVE), and the pilot fell through each time to the step it
    *could* evaluate — which is the last one, because the last step of a discard order is "a
    counterspell". Two of those three windows are two of that seat's five losses. The control is in
    the same seat: `125v123` s112 sent two Islands, which is what the other three windows needed.
    The step now reads the battlefield header's own printed `and N are lands`. #199 established
    that the step which WINS is step 0; this is its companion at the other end of the list.
    (deck125 S2; extends #189 and #193 to ordered procedures.)

216. **A RUNG BREAK REQUIRES THAT A BETTER ROW EXISTED ON THE SAME SCREEN, AND "NO ALTERNATIVE
    EXISTED" IS ITS OWN VERDICT — NEITHER PASS NOR FAIL. REPORT `N raw / M live / K consequential`
    AND SCORE K, THEN WRITE THE EXEMPTIONS INTO THE GUIDE.** Two seats found this independently and
    every count in the pool moved when it was applied. deck130 cast land destruction past its own
    gate three times in `130v146` (s44, s47, s60) — and every one of those prompts reads
    `Your hand (1 card)` with that card the only legal cast; scored as breaks they would have
    bought an edit that could not change a decision. deck125's tap-out gate: **5 raw, 1 live** (the
    other four are a sweeper at a header of 5, a sweeper at 4, an Elixir activation at 2 life, and
    a turn-1 cast holding a 5-mana counter no board could have cast). deck125's Path rule: **2 raw,
    0 live** (both "1-power" bodies had repeating text). deck126's D92: **73 raw, 5 live, 0
    consequential** — 65 of the 73 are turns 26-28 of a game won 41-0 in which every cast row was
    engine-dead. Rule: before recording a break, read the hand line and the menu; report the three
    numbers; and put the exemption in the GUIDE TEXT, because an exemption that lives only in a
    seat file has to be rediscovered every wave. (deck125 S3 + deck130 S6; extends #201 and #198.)

217. **WHEN A SEAT'S WINDOW COUNT MOVES BY MORE THAN A FACTOR, EVERY PER-WINDOW RATE AT THAT SEAT
    IS SUSPECT BEFORE IT IS EVIDENCE — SAY SO AT THE TOP OF THE SEAT FILE AND MARK THE RATES
    INCOMPARABLE.** deck125 went 4-1 to 1-5 while its decisions fell **1,075 -> 405** and its
    opponent-turn windows **479 -> 109** against a turn count that fell only 261 -> 169; in
    `125v130` a draw-go deck received **one** opponent-turn window in twenty turns. The cause is an
    engine defect and three of the five losses carry no identifiable misplay; no edit was written
    for them, which is the right answer. Corpus-wide the same instrument moved the class denominator
    on its own: total decisions fell 36% (3,483 -> 2,212) while opponent-turn ask/priority windows
    fell **58%** (1,052 -> 441) — the opponent-turn SHARE of all decisions fell from 30.2% to 19.9%,
    a collapse the general shrinkage does not explain. Rule: the NEW-BASELINE discipline (never
    attribute win-rate variance to guide edits) has a sibling that is not about hands — compare
    this corpus's windows PER SEAT-TURN against the last one, and a ceiling that "held 40/40" on a
    denominator of 155 last corpus is not the same evidence. **This is #188's denominator discipline
    applied to the corpus rather than to a literal, and this wave it decided which lane predictions
    could be scored at all.** (deck125 S4; the adjudication is in `general-strategy.md` R193.)

218. **A CLAUSE THE PILOT KEEPS OBEYING *AGAINST* YOUR INSTRUCTION IS A CLAUSE IT HAS A THEORY
    ABOUT, AND THE GUIDE ANSWERS THE THEORY BEFORE IT REPEATS THE INSTRUCTION.** deck126's Rule #7
    entry 1 already read: take the missing enchantment "at any `leaves N`, including
    `casting this taps you out`". The pilot broke it twice and **both breaks are on that exact
    clause** — `126v146` seq 14 at 25 life (declined `Cast Sanguine Bond … casting this taps you
    out` for a Perimeter Captain at `leaves 4`; the Bond arrived six turns later and the game was
    lost by 5 life) and `126v162` seq 11. The rule had told it the clause was not a stop, in the
    clause's own words, and it still read the clause as a stop. The theory is "tapping out is
    dangerous", which is true in most decks and false in this one: deck126 holds one instant, has
    no counterspell, and blocks with defenders whether its lands are tapped or not. The edit says
    THAT, then restates the instruction. Companion to #174's always-false device and to #197.
    (deck126 S5.)

219. **THE OPPONENT'S BATTLEFIELD LINE IS ONE OF THE DEDICATED LINES A GUIDE MUST READ WHENEVER A
    TAG THERE CHANGES THE PRICE OF ONE OF *YOUR* ROWS. THE REVIEW QUESTION THAT FINDS THESE: FOR
    EACH NEW RENDER, ASK WHOSE LIFE IT MOVES, THEN CHECK WHETHER THAT SEAT'S GUIDE READS THE LINE
    IT IS PRINTED ON.** Silverquill Silencer (`borderline.txt:102764`,
    `auto=chooseanameopp transforms((,newability[@movedto(*[chosenname]|opponentstack):life:-3
    opponent && draw:1 controller]))`) prints its chosen name on the OPPONENT battlefield line as
    `[named: <card>]`. The tag rendered **54 times** across two seats and is complete and correct —
    but every guide rule about "read your battlefield line" and "read the row you are answering"
    points somewhere else, and the cast row does not price it. deck126 cast the named card **2 of
    2** times it cast it at all, for 3 life each, in a game it lost by 5 (`126v146` seq 42 at 24 ->
    21 and seq 61 at 8 -> 5). **Sizing, and it is why this is one bullet and not a section** (#198):
    the same tag sat as `[named: Chromatic Lantern]` for 19 records and `[named: Essence Scatter]`
    for 12 with ZERO casts of either — the pilot only walks into it when the named card is the card
    the deck's whole plan is about. (deck126 S6; the render half is an R-item, and the two are not
    substitutes.)

220. **A WAVE IN WHICH A GUIDE'S PREDICTIONS ALL PASS IS THE WAVE TO WRITE THE FEWEST LINES, AND A
    CLOSED LANE'S "WHAT THIS COST" RECITAL IS THE BYTE BUDGET'S NATURAL DONOR — RETIRED IN THE SAME
    WAVE ITS PREDICTION PASSES BOTH HALVES, WITH THE SEAT FILE NAMING THE EDIT THAT SPENT THE
    BYTES.** deck126 passed D92-D98 (the zero-Tribute stop 2/39 -> **0/99**, the dead-tutor stop
    2/22 -> **0/3**, the second-copy stop 1/3 -> **0/24**, reveal picks 7/9 -> **10/10**, blockers
    0 `BLOCKS: none` of 15, land drop 46/46) and wrote **three** edits. deck162's first-Mine
    over-brake lane passed both halves (untagged declines 1 of 4, and that one a punisher collision;
    tagged takes at K of 0: 0 of 1) and its eleven-window recital had nothing left to buy — retiring
    it paid for that guide's two new findings almost exactly. Growth in a passing guide is
    uncompensated risk: every added sentence is a new surface for the #202/#178 over-aggression
    failure, and this wave's #206 mirror is what that looks like when it fires. The rule a recital
    justifies always STAYS; only the recital goes. (deck126 S7 + deck152 S6; companion to #200(c).)

221. **WHEN A RULE'S PRIMARY BRANCH IS KEYED TO AN *OPTIONAL* ANNOTATION, THE GUIDE STATES THE
    CONDITION UNDER WHICH IT PRINTS AND CARRIES A COMPLETE BRANCH FOR ITS ABSENCE — AND THE
    REVIEWER REPORTS THE MARKER'S *RENDER* COUNT, NOT ONLY ITS TAKE RATE.** deck130's whole X rung
    is built on `[<- most kills at any affordable X that costs you nothing]`. That string rendered
    **0 times in the entire 42-log corpus** (grepped across every `.jsonl`, re-derived by this
    step). It prints only when some affordable X kills something of theirs and nothing of yours,
    which held on neither X menu at that seat nor anywhere else. The guide's fallback ("find the row
    whose YOURS reads none") assumes such a row exists; at `130v152` s17, at 9 life against 25, none
    did, the rule had no branch, and the pilot answered `X = 1 {kills THEIRS: none; YOURS: Goblin
    x3}` — sweeping its own board, killing nothing of theirs, and losing the game two windows later.
    **Wave 53 scored that rung "taken 2/2" and predicted N/N again: a rung marked PASS twice on a
    surface that had stopped printing.** `2 of 2 taken` and `0 of 0 rendered` are the same number on
    paper and opposite findings. (deck130 S5; this is the sharpest instance in eleven corpora of the
    silent-instrument shape — a missing metric and a passing test producing identical output.)

222. **BOTTOMING IS REPORTED AS OFFERS / SHIPS / BOTTOMS WITH THE *ORDER THE REPLY IMPLIES*, AND NO
    VERDICT, UNTIL THE SAMPLE SUPPORTS ONE.** This is the first corpus with a meaningful number of
    real `bottom` records (**8**, against 5 last wave) and the guides' bottoming sections are
    PREFERENCE ORDERS: two or three samples cannot discriminate an order, and a lucky two-for-two
    reads as a validated one. deck123's two bottoms were both correct and one won its game, which
    tells us nothing yet; deck152, deck162 and deck146 supplied four more, all sending the most
    expensive card the keep could not cast. Extend #200's UNTESTABLE-AT-THIS-SEAT machinery from
    the mulligan half to the bottoming half explicitly. (deck130 S7. deck130 itself shipped 0
    mulligans and 0 bottoms for a FOURTH corpus and stays #132-UNTESTABLE-AT-THIS-SEAT.)

223. **A DECISION CLASS THE PILOT HANDLED *CORRECTLY* AND ONLY FROM A RENDER CLAUSE THAT IS NEW
    THIS CORPUS IS A FINDING WITH A SENTENCE OWED — FILED AS "WHAT THIS BOUGHT" — AND THE SENTENCE
    STATES THE SCOPE THE PILOT LEFT UNSTATED.** Four windows at `146v162` (s46 at 8 life, s49 at 7,
    s53 at 8, s55 at 6) declined full cast menus off lane C's brand-new
    `[DRAW PRICE: casting this draws YOU 7 cards (their Forced Fruition), and their Underworld
    Dreams deals you 7 - you would be at 1]`, with **no guide sentence about it anywhere**, and the
    seat won that game at 4 life on attacks alone. A seat file that records only breaks writes
    nothing here and the next Forced Fruition seat rolls the same die. The scope half is the point
    and the same game proves it: the tax is on SPELLS, so attacks, land drops and loyalty abilities
    remain free — which is exactly how that game was won under the same tax the pilot correctly
    refused to pay for a spell. (deck146 S2. Corpus-wide this wave: 43 DRAW PRICE rows, **43 with
    the `- you would be at K` tail**, 9 carrying `this KILLS you`, **0 casts from any of them**.)

224. **IN A RANKED-ORDER INSTRUCTION, ANY RUNG EXPRESSED AS A SUPERLATIVE NAMES THE *RENDERED FIELD*
    IT IS A SUPERLATIVE OVER, OR IT IS NOT A RUNG.** deck146's cleanup order named its top cards
    explicitly (Emeria's Call, Agadeem's Awakening, a second planeswalker) and the named half PASSED
    1/1 (`146v125` s20, Emeria's Call at row 6, `PUT: 6`). Its unnamed tail — "then the priciest
    spell" — broke **2 of 7**, both times sending a `{2}{b}` card while a `{3}{b}{b}` or `{3}{b}{w}`
    sat on the same numbered list with its cost printed on the row. Named-card rungs verify;
    superlative rungs over an unnamed field do not, because the pilot must first decide what the
    superlative ranges over. (deck146 S3; the same shape as #215 one level down.)

225. **WHEN A CORPUS SHOWS A BREAK UNDER A RULE THAT ALREADY RENDERS AND IS ALREADY CORRECTLY
    KEYED, THE EDIT THAT IS ALLOWED IS A RECOGNISE->DO ENTRY NAMING THE *WRONG ANSWER* AND WHAT IT
    COSTS — NEVER A THIRD STATEMENT OF THE RIGHT ONE.** #181 gates restatement on whether a rule
    protected anything; this is the rung past that. `152v146` s58, the corpus's ONLY
    `all_assignments_illegal`: two menace 2/1 Spiders, two blockers, at 6 life against a header
    reading `Unblocked, these attackers deal up to 6 - you would be at 0 - LETHAL`. The menace rule
    was printed THREE times — on each A-row and inside each B-row's per-attacker parenthesis
    (`no 1-on-1 result exists - only a block by TWO OR MORE of your creatures counts; this one alone
    does not block it at all`) — and the guide already carries the affordance sentence keyed to that
